The graph assumes every tensor in the captured op sequence\\\\n  has the same size and layout in every replay.\\\\n* Using multiple streams in a capture is allowed, but there are :ref:`restrictions<multistream-capture>`.\\\\n\\\\nNon-constraints\\\\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\\\\n\\\\n* Once captured, the graph may be replayed on any stream.\\\\n\\\\n.. _whole-network-capture:\\\\n\\\\nWhole-network capture\\\\n^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^\\\\n\\\\nIf your entire network is capturable, you can capture and replay an entire iteration::\\\\n\\\\n    N, D_in, H, D_out = 640, 4096, 2048, 1024\\\\n    model = torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Linear(D_in, H),\\\\n                                torch.nn.Dropout(p=0.2),\\\\n                                torch.nn.Linear(H, D_out),\\\\n                                torch.nn.Dropout(p=0.1)).cuda()\\\\n    loss_fn = torch.nn.MSELoss()\\\\n    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)\\\\n\\\\n    # Placeholders used for capture\\\\n    static_input = torch.randn(N, D_in, device='cuda')\\\\n    static_target = torch.randn(N, D_out, device='cuda')\\\\n\\\\n    # warmup\\\\n    # Uses static_input and static_target here for convenience,\\\\n    # but in a real setting, because the warmup includes optimizer.step()\\\\n    # you must use a few batches of real data.\\\\n    s = torch.cuda.Stream()\\\\n    s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())\\\\n    with torch.cuda.stream(s):\\\\n        for i in range(3):\\\\n            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)\\\\n            y_pred = model(static_input)\\\\n            loss = loss_fn(y_pred, static_target)\\\\n            loss.backward()\\\\n            optimizer.step()\\\\n    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)\\\\n\\\\n    # capture\\\\n    g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()\\\\n    # Sets grads to None before capture, so backward() will create\\\\n    # .grad attributes with allocations from the graph's private pool\\\\n    optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)\\\\n    with torch.cuda.graph(g):\\\\n        static_y_pred = model(static_input)\\\\n        static_loss = loss_fn(static_y_pred, static_target)\\\\n        static_loss.backward()\\\\n        optimizer.step()\\\\n\\\\n    real_inputs = [torch.rand_like(static_input) for _ in range(10)]\\\\n    real_targets = [torch.rand_like(static_target) for _ in range(10)]\\\\n\\\\n    for data, target in zip(real_inputs, real_targets):\\\\n        # Fills the graph's input memory with new data to compute on\\\\n        static_input.copy_(data)\\\\n        static_target.copy_(target)\\\\n        # replay() includes forward, backward, and step.\\\\n        # You don't even need to call optimizer.zero_grad() between iterations\\\\n        # because the captured backward refills static .grad tensors in place.\\\\n        g.replay()\\\\n        # Params have been updated. static_y_pred, static_loss, and .grad\\\\n        # attributes hold values from computing on this iteration's data.\\\\n\\\\n.. _partial-network-capture:\\\\n\\\\nPartial-network capture\\\\n^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^\\\\n\\\\nIf some of your network is unsafe to capture (e.g., due to dynamic control flow,\\\\ndynamic shapes, CPU syncs, or essential CPU-side logic), you can run the unsafe\\\\npart(s) eagerly and use :func:`torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables` to graph only\\\\nthe capture-safe part(s).\\\\n\\\\nBy default, callables returned by :func:`~torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables`\\\\nare autograd-aware, and can be used in the training loop as direct replacements\\\\nfor the functions or :class:`nn.Module<torch.nn.Module>`\\\\\\\\ s you passed.\\\\n\\\\n:func:`~torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables` internally creates\\\\n:class:`~torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` objects, runs warmup iterations, and maintains\\\\nstatic inputs and outputs as needed.  Therefore (unlike with\\\\n:class:`torch.cuda.graph`) you don't need to handle those manually.\\\\n\\\\nIn the following example, data-dependent dynamic control flow means the\\\\nnetwork isn't capturable end-to-end, but\\\\n:func:`~torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables`\\\\nlets us capture and run graph-safe sections as graphs regardless::\\\\n\\\\n    N, D_in, H, D_out = 640, 4096, 2048, 1024\\\\n\\\\n    module1 = torch.nn.Linear(D_in, H).cuda()\\\\n    module2 = torch.nn.Linear(H, D_out).cuda()\\\\n    module3 = torch.nn.Linear(H, D_out).cuda()\\\\n\\\\n    loss_fn = torch.nn.MSELoss()\\\\n    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(chain(module1.parameters(),\\\\n                                      module2.parameters(),\\\\n                                      module3.parameters()),\\\\n                                lr=0.1)\\\\n\\\\n    # Sample inputs used for capture\\\\n    # requires_grad state of sample inputs must match\\\\n    # requires_grad state of real inputs each callable will see.\\\\n    x = torch.randn(N, D_in, device='cuda')\\\\n    h = torch.randn(N, H, device='cuda', requires_grad=True)\\\\n\\\\n    module1 = torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables(module1, (x,))\\\\n    module2 = torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables(module2, (h,))\\\\n    module3 = torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables(module3, (h,))\\\\n\\\\n    real_inputs = [torch.rand_like(x) for _ in range(10)]\\\\n    real_targets = [torch.randn(N, D_out, device=\\\\\\\"cuda\\\\\\\") for _ in range(10)]\\\\n\\\\n    for data, target in zip(real_inputs, real_targets):\\\\n        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)\\\\n\\\\n        tmp = module1(data)  # forward ops run as a graph\\\\n\\\\n        if tmp.sum().item() > 0:\\\\n            tmp = module2(tmp)  # forward ops run as a graph\\\\n        else:\\\\n            tmp = module3(tmp)  # forward ops run as a graph\\\\n\\\\n        loss = loss_fn(tmp, target)\\\\n        # module2's or module3's (whichever was chosen) backward ops,\\\\n        # as well as module1's backward ops, run as graphs\\\\n        loss.backward()\\\\n        optimizer.step()\\\\n\\\\n.. _graphs-with-amp:\\\\n\\\\nUsage with torch.cuda.amp\\\\n^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^\\\\n\\\\nFor typical optimizers, :meth:`GradScaler.step<torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler.step>` syncs\\\\nthe CPU with the GPU, which is prohibited during capture. To avoid errors, either use\\\\n:ref:`partial-network capture<partial-network-capture>`, or (if forward, loss,\\\\nand backward are capture-safe) capture forward, loss, and backward but not the\\\\noptimizer step::\\\\n\\\\n    # warmup\\\\n    # In a real setting, use a few batches of real data.\\\\n    s = torch.cuda.Stream()\\\\n    s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())\\\\n    with torch.cuda.stream(s):\\\\n        for i in range(3):\\\\n            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)\\\\n            with torch.cuda.amp.autocast():\\\\n                y_pred = model(static_input)\\\\n                loss = loss_fn(y_pred, static_target)\\\\n            scaler.scale(loss).backward()\\\\n            scaler.step(optimizer)\\\\n            scaler.update()\\\\n    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)\\\\n\\\\n    # capture\\\\n    g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()\\\\n    optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)\\\\n    with torch.cuda.graph(g):\\\\n        with torch.cuda.amp.autocast():\\\\n            static_y_pred = model(static_input)\\\\n            static_loss = loss_fn(static_y_pred, static_target)\\\\n        scaler.scale(static_loss).backward()\\\\n        # don't capture scaler.step(optimizer) or scaler.update()\\\\n\\\\n    real_inputs = [torch.rand_like(static_input) for _ in range(10)]\\\\n    real_targets = [torch.rand_like(static_target) for _ in range(10)]\\\\n\\\\n    for data, target in zip(real_inputs, real_targets):\\\\n        static_input.copy_(data)\\\\n        static_target.copy_(target)\\\\n        g.replay()\\\\n        # Runs scaler.step and scaler.update eagerly\\\\n        scaler.step(optimizer)\\\\n        scaler.update()\\\\n\\\\n.. _multistream-capture:\\\\n\\\\nUsage with multiple streams\\\\n^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^\\\\n\\\\nCapture mode automatically propagates to any streams that sync with a capturing stream.\\\\nWithin capture, you may expose parallelism by issuing calls to different streams,\\\\nbut the overall stream dependency DAG must branch out from the\\\\ninitial capturing stream after capture begins and rejoin the initial stream\\\\nbefore capture ends::\\\\n\\\\n    with torch.cuda.graph(g):\\\\n        # at context manager entrance, torch.cuda.current_stream()\\\\n        # is the initial capturing stream\\\\n\\\\n        # INCORRECT (does not branch out from or rejoin initial stream)\\\\n        with torch.cuda.stream(s):\\\\n            cuda_work()\\\\n\\\\n        # CORRECT:\\\\n        # branches out from initial stream\\\\n        s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())\\\\n        with torch.cuda.stream(s):\\\\n            cuda_work()\\\\n        # rejoins initial stream before capture ends\\\\n        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)\\\\n\\\\n.. note::\\\\n\\\\n    To avoid confusion for power users looking at replays in nsight systems or nvprof:\\\\n    Unlike eager execution, the graph interprets a nontrivial stream DAG in capture\\\\n    as a hint, not a command. During replay, the graph may reorganize independent ops\\\\n    onto different streams or enqueue them in a different order (while respecting your\\\\n    original DAG's overall dependencies).\\\\n\\\\nUsage with DistributedDataParallel\\\\n^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^\\\\n\\\\nNCCL < 2.9.6\\\\n~~~~~~~~~~~~\\\\n\\\\nNCCL versions earlier than 2.9.6 don't allow collectives to be captured.\\\\nYou must use :ref:`partial-network capture<partial-network-capture>`,\\\\nwhich defers allreduces to happen outside graphed sections of backward.\\\\n\\\\nCall :func:`~torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables` on graphable network sections\\\\n*before* wrapping the network with DDP.\\\\n\\\\nNCCL >= 2.9.6\\\\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~\\\\n\\\\nNCCL versions 2.9.6 or later allow collectives in the graph.\\\\nApproaches that capture an :ref:`entire backward pass<whole-network-capture>`\\\\nare a viable option, but need three setup steps.\\\\n\\\\n1. Disable DDP's internal async error handling::\\\\n\\\\n    os.environ[\\\\\\\"NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING\\\\\\\"] = \\\\\\\"0\\\\\\\"\\\\n    torch.distributed.init_process_group(...)\\\\n\\\\n2. Before full-backward capture, DDP must be constructed in a side-stream context::\\\\n\\\\n    with torch.cuda.stream(s):\\\\n        model = DistributedDataParallel(model)\\\\n\\\\n3. Your warmup must run at least 11 DDP-enabled eager iterations before capture.\\\\n\\\\n.. _graph-memory-management:\\\\n\\\\nGraph memory management\\\\n^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^\\\\n\\\\nA captured graph acts on the same virtual addresses every time it replays.\\\\nIf PyTorch frees the memory, a later replay can hit an illegal memory access.\\\\nIf PyTorch reassigns the memory to new tensors, the replay can corrupt the values\\\\nseen by those tensors.  Therefore, the virtual addresses used by the graph must be\\\\nreserved for the graph across replays. The PyTorch caching allocator achieves this\\\\nby detecting when capture is underway and satisfying the capture's allocations\\\\nfrom a graph-private memory pool. The private pool stays alive until its\\\\n:class:`~torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` object and all tensors created during capture\\\\ngo out of scope.\\\\n\\\\nPrivate pools are maintained automatically. By default, the allocator creates a\\\\nseparate private pool for each capture. If you capture multiple graphs,\\\\nthis conservative approach ensures graph replays never corrupt each other's values,\\\\nbut sometimes needlessly wastes memory.\\\\n\\\\nSharing memory across captures\\\\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\\\\n\\\\nTo economize the memory stashed in private pools, :class:`torch.cuda.graph`\\\\nand :func:`torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables` optionally allow different\\\\ncaptures to share the same private pool.\\\\nIt's safe for a set of graphs to share a private pool if you know they'll always\\\\nbe replayed in the same order they were captured,\\\\nand never be replayed concurrently.\\\\n\\\\n:class:`torch.cuda.graph`'s ``pool`` argument is a hint to use a particular private pool,\\\\nand can be used to share memory across graphs as shown::\\\\n\\\\n    g1 = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()\\\\n    g2 = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()\\\\n\\\\n    # (create static inputs for g1 and g2, run warmups of their workloads...)\\\\n\\\\n    # Captures g1\\\\n    with torch.cuda.graph(g1):\\\\n        static_out_1 = g1_workload(static_in_1)\\\\n\\\\n    # Captures g2, hinting that g2 may share a memory pool with g1\\\\n    with torch.cuda.graph(g2, pool=g1.pool()):\\\\n        static_out_2 = g2_workload(static_in_2)\\\\n\\\\n    static_in_1.copy_(real_data_1)\\\\n    static_in_2.copy_(real_data_2)\\\\n    g1.replay()\\\\n    g2.replay()\\\\n\\\\nIt's also safe to share a memory pool across separate graphs that do not depend\\\\non each other's outputs, provided they never run concurrently.\\\\nBe aware that replaying one graph can clobber another graph's outputs when\\\\nthey share a pool, unless :meth:`~torch.Tensor.clone` is called on the outputs\\\\nbeforehand.\\\\nThis pattern is frequently used in inference servers that accept variable batch\\\\nsizes at runtime.\\\\nvLLM is a notable example; see `here <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/938a81692ea318e59ead4750e7e7425bfd6a4896/vllm/platforms/interface.py#L508-L515>`__\\\\nand `here <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/938a81692ea318e59ead4750e7e7425bfd6a4896/vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py#L86-L89>`__.\\\\n\\\\nWith :func:`torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables`, if you want to graph several\\\\ncallables and you know they'll always run in the same order (and never concurrently)\\\\npass them as a tuple in the same order they'll run in the live workload, and\\\\n:func:`~torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables` will capture their graphs using a shared\\\\nprivate pool.\\\\n\\\\nIf, in the live workload, your callables will run in an order that occasionally changes,\\\\nor if they'll run concurrently, passing them as a tuple to a single invocation of\\\\n:func:`~torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables` is not allowed. Instead, you must call\\\\n:func:`~torch.cuda.make_graphed_callables` separately for each one.\\\\n\\\\n.. _graph-data-dependent-control-flow:\\\\n\\\\nData Dependent Control Flow\\\\n^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^\\\\n\\\\nData-dependent control flow can with cuda graphs if the control flow\\\\nis implemented using torch.cond(). If your function uses this\\\\nfunction, compiling it with the \\\\\\\"cudagraphs\\\\\\\" backend will enable\\\\ncontrol flow in the resulting cuda graph via `conditional nodes`_.\\\\n\\\\nDoing cuda graph capture of eager mode code using torch.cond() will\\\\nalso work.\\\\n\\\\nSupport for inductor backend to torch.compile is not available yet,\\\\nbut there is no fundamental blocker.\\\\n\\\\nAn example of using the cudagraphs backend to torch.compile on code\\\\nusing torch.cond is demonstrated below::\\\\n\\\\n    import torch\\\\n\\\\n    def true_fn(x):\\\\n        return x.sin()\\\\n\\\\n    def false_fn(x):\\\\n        return x.cos()\\\\n\\\\n    x = torch.randn(4, device=\\\\\\\"cuda\\\\\\\", requires_grad=False)\\\\n    pred = torch.tensor(False, device=\\\\\\\"cuda\\\\\\\", requires_grad=False)\\\\n    def foo(pred, x):\\\\n        with torch.inference_mode():\\\\n            return torch.cond(pred, true_fn, false_fn, [x])\\\\n\\\\n    # First call will run eager for warmup, second call will do graph\\\\n    # capture followed by graph replay, third call and beyond will do\\\\n    # just graph replay.\\\\n    compiled_foo = torch.compile(foo, backend=\\\\\\\"cudagraphs\\\\\\\")\\\\n    for i in range(3):\\\\n        y = compiled_foo(pred, x)\\\\n\\\\n    # will output x.sin()\\\\n    y = compiled_foo(~pred, x)\\\\n\\\", \\\"excerpt_ranges\\\": [[0, 80851]], \\\"range_unit\\\": \\\"zero-based half-open characters in extracted text\\\", \\\"extracted_characters\\\": 80851, \\\"selected_characters\\\": 80851, \\\"extraction\\\": \\\"UTF-8 text\\\", \\\"selection_reason\\\": \\\"full extracted text fits allocation\\\"}, {\\\"path\\\": \\\"references/S-TORCH-REPRO/fulltext.txt\\\", \\\"sha256\\\": \\\"4f6b1deb38f7f174a2e340674680aaa0484e02a1d18cccd1bb94618df512cc2a\\\", \\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"source_original\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"\\\\n===== docs/source/notes/randomness.rst =====\\\\n.. _reproducibility:\\\\n\\\\nReproducibility\\\\n===============\\\\n\\\\nCompletely reproducible results are not guaranteed across PyTorch releases,\\\\nindividual commits, or different platforms. Furthermore, results may not be\\\\nreproducible between CPU and GPU executions, even when using identical seeds.\\\\n\\\\nHowever, there are some steps you can take to limit the number of sources of\\\\nnondeterministic behavior for a specific platform, device, and PyTorch release.\\\\nFirst, you can control sources of randomness that can cause multiple executions\\\\nof your application to behave differently. Second, you can configure PyTorch\\\\nto avoid using nondeterministic algorithms for some operations, so that multiple\\\\ncalls to those operations, given the same inputs, will produce the same result.\\\\n\\\\n.. warning::\\\\n\\\\n    Deterministic operations are often slower than nondeterministic operations, so\\\\n    single-run performance may decrease for your model. However, determinism may\\\\n    save time in development by facilitating experimentation, debugging, and\\\\n    regression testing.\\\\n\\\\nControlling sources of randomness\\\\n.................................\\\\n\\\\nPyTorch random number generator\\\\n-------------------------------\\\\nYou can use :meth:`torch.manual_seed()` to seed the RNG for all devices (both\\\\nCPU and CUDA)::\\\\n\\\\n    import torch\\\\n    torch.manual_seed(0)\\\\n\\\\nSome PyTorch operations may use random numbers internally.\\\\n:meth:`torch.svd_lowrank()` does this, for instance. Consequently, calling it\\\\nmultiple times back-to-back with the same input arguments may give different\\\\nresults. However, as long as :meth:`torch.manual_seed()` is set to a constant\\\\nat the beginning of an application and all other sources of nondeterminism have\\\\nbeen eliminated, the same series of random numbers will be generated each time\\\\nthe application is run in the same environment.\\\\n\\\\nIt is also possible to obtain identical results from an operation that uses\\\\nrandom numbers by setting :meth:`torch.manual_seed()` to the same value between\\\\nsubsequent calls.\\\\n\\\\nPython\\\\n------\\\\n\\\\nFor custom operators, you might need to set python seed as well::\\\\n\\\\n    import random\\\\n    random.seed(0)\\\\n\\\\nRandom number generators in other libraries\\\\n-------------------------------------------\\\\nIf you or any of the libraries you are using rely on NumPy, you can seed the global\\\\nNumPy RNG with::\\\\n\\\\n    import numpy as np\\\\n    np.random.seed(0)\\\\n\\\\nHowever, some applications and libraries may use NumPy Random Generator objects,\\\\nnot the global RNG\\\\n(`<https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/random/generator.html>`_), and those will\\\\nneed to be seeded consistently as well.\\\\n\\\\nIf you are using any other libraries that use random number generators, refer to\\\\nthe documentation for those libraries to see how to set consistent seeds for them.\\\\n\\\\nCUDA convolution benchmarking\\\\n-----------------------------\\\\nThe cuDNN library, used by CUDA convolution operations, can be a source of nondeterminism\\\\nacross multiple executions of an application. When a cuDNN convolution is called with a\\\\nnew set of size parameters, an optional feature can run multiple convolution algorithms,\\\\nbenchmarking them to find the fastest one. Then, the fastest algorithm will be used\\\\nconsistently during the rest of the process for the corresponding set of size parameters.\\\\nDue to benchmarking noise and different hardware, the benchmark may select different\\\\nalgorithms on subsequent runs, even on the same machine.\\\\n\\\\nDisabling the benchmarking feature with :code:`torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False`\\\\ncauses cuDNN to deterministically select an algorithm, possibly at the cost of reduced\\\\nperformance.\\\\n\\\\nHowever, if you do not need reproducibility across multiple executions of your application,\\\\nthen performance might improve if the benchmarking feature is enabled with\\\\n:code:`torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True`.\\\\n\\\\nNote that this setting is different from the :code:`torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic`\\\\nsetting discussed below.\\\\n\\\\nAvoiding nondeterministic algorithms\\\\n....................................\\\\n:meth:`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms` lets you configure PyTorch to use\\\\ndeterministic algorithms instead of nondeterministic ones where available, and\\\\nto throw an error if an operation is known to be nondeterministic (and without\\\\na deterministic alternative).\\\\n\\\\nPlease check the documentation for :meth:`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms()`\\\\nfor a full list of affected operations. If an operation does not act correctly\\\\naccording to the documentation, or if you need a deterministic implementation\\\\nof an operation that does not have one, please submit an issue:\\\\n`<https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues?q=label:%22module:%20determinism%22>`_\\\\n\\\\nFor example, running the nondeterministic CUDA implementation of :meth:`torch.Tensor.index_add_`\\\\nwill throw an error::\\\\n\\\\n    >>> import torch\\\\n    >>> torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)\\\\n    >>> torch.randn(2, 2).cuda().index_add_(0, torch.tensor([0, 1]), torch.randn(2, 2))\\\\n    Traceback (most recent call last):\\\\n    File \\\\\\\"<stdin>\\\\\\\", line 1, in <module>\\\\n    RuntimeError: index_add_cuda_ does not have a deterministic implementation, but you set\\\\n    'torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)'. ...\\\\n\\\\nWhen :meth:`torch.bmm` is called with sparse-dense CUDA tensors it typically uses a\\\\nnondeterministic algorithm, but when the deterministic flag is turned on, its alternate\\\\ndeterministic implementation will be used::\\\\n\\\\n    >>> import torch\\\\n    >>> torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)\\\\n    >>> torch.bmm(torch.randn(2, 2, 2).to_sparse().cuda(), torch.randn(2, 2, 2).cuda())\\\\n    tensor([[[ 1.1900, -2.3409],\\\\n             [ 0.4796,  0.8003]],\\\\n            [[ 0.1509,  1.8027],\\\\n             [ 0.0333, -1.1444]]], device='cuda:0')\\\\n\\\\nCUDA convolution determinism\\\\n----------------------------\\\\nWhile disabling CUDA convolution benchmarking (discussed above) ensures that\\\\nCUDA selects the same algorithm each time an application is run, that algorithm\\\\nitself may be nondeterministic, unless either\\\\n:code:`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` or\\\\n:code:`torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True` is set. The latter setting\\\\ncontrols only this behavior, unlike :meth:`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms`\\\\nwhich will make other PyTorch operations behave deterministically, too.\\\\n\\\\nCUDA RNN and LSTM\\\\n-----------------\\\\nIn some versions of CUDA, RNNs and LSTM networks may have non-deterministic behavior.\\\\nSee :meth:`torch.nn.RNN` and :meth:`torch.nn.LSTM` for details and workarounds.\\\\n\\\\nFilling uninitialized memory\\\\n----------------------------\\\\nOperations like :meth:`torch.empty` and :meth:`torch.Tensor.resize_` can return\\\\ntensors with uninitialized memory that contain undefined values. Using such a\\\\ntensor as an input to another operation is invalid if determinism is required,\\\\nbecause the output will be nondeterministic. But there is nothing to actually\\\\nprevent such invalid code from being run. So for safety,\\\\n:attr:`torch.utils.deterministic.fill_uninitialized_memory` is set to ``True``\\\\nby default, which will fill the uninitialized memory with a known value if\\\\n:code:`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` is set. This will prevent the\\\\npossibility of this kind of nondeterministic behavior.\\\\n\\\\nHowever, filling uninitialized memory is detrimental to performance. So if your\\\\nprogram is valid and does not use uninitialized memory as the input to an\\\\noperation, then this setting can be turned off for better performance.\\\\n\\\\nDataLoader\\\\n..........\\\\n\\\\nDataLoader will reseed workers following :ref:`data-loading-randomness` algorithm.\\\\nUse :meth:`worker_init_fn` and `generator` to preserve reproducibility::\\\\n\\\\n    def seed_worker(worker_id):\\\\n        worker_seed = torch.initial_seed() % 2**32\\\\n        numpy.random.seed(worker_seed)\\\\n        random.seed(worker_seed)\\\\n\\\\n    g = torch.Generator()\\\\n    g.manual_seed(0)\\\\n\\\\n    DataLoader(\\\\n        train_dataset,\\\\n        batch_size=batch_size,\\\\n        num_workers=num_workers,\\\\n        worker_init_fn=seed_worker,\\\\n        generator=g,\\\\n    )\\\\n\\\", \\\"excerpt_ranges\\\": [[0, 7936]], \\\"range_unit\\\": \\\"zero-based half-open \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"source_original\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"\\\\n===== docs/source/user_guide/torch_compiler/torch.compiler_dynamic_shapes.md =====\\\\n---\\\\nfile_format: mystnb\\\\nkernelspec:\\\\n  name: python3\\\\nmystnb:\\\\n  execution_timeout: 30\\\\n  execution_show_tb: True\\\\n  merge_streams: True\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n```{code-cell}\\\\n:tags: [remove-cell]\\\\nimport torch\\\\nfrom compile import header_code\\\\n\\\\ntorch._logging.set_logs(graph_breaks=True, graph_code=True)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n(dynamic_shapes)=\\\\n# Dynamic Shapes\\\\n\\\\nThis section explains how to work with dynamic shapes in PyTorch, including how\\\\nto debug and fix common errors, implement support for dynamic shapes in\\\\noperators, and understand the underlying mechanisms.\\\\n\\\\nDynamic shapes allow PyTorch models to handle inputs with varying dimensions\\\\nwithout recompilation. This enables more flexible models that can process\\\\ndifferent batch sizes, sequence lengths, or image dimensions in a single\\\\ncompiled artifact. Dynamic shapes work by symbolically tracing tensor\\\\ndimensions rather than using concrete values, creating a computation\\\\ngraph that adapts to different input shapes at runtime. By default,\\\\nPyTorch assumes all input shapes to be static.\\\\n\\\\nTypically, deep learning compilers only support static shapes, requiring\\\\nrecompilation for input shape changes. While this approach covers many use cases,\\\\nthere are situations where this is insufficient:\\\\n\\\\n- **Variable Dimensions** - Batch sizes or sequence lengths vary, such as in\\\\nadaptive batching.\\\\n- **Data-Dependent Outputs** - Models produce outputs based on input data,\\\\nlike variable bounding boxes in detection models.\\\\n- **Sparse Representations** - Processing depends on data-varying sparse structures,\\\\nsuch as in sparse tensors, jagged tensors, and graph neural networks.\\\\n\\\\nDynamic shapes do not support dynamic rank programs, programs which input tensors\\\\nchange in dimensionality, as this is uncommon and unnecessarily complex.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n## What does it mean for a size/integer to be dynamic?\\\\n\\\\nDynamic shapes allow avoiding recompilations by making certain dimensions or integers\\\\ndynamic. For example, if a function `f(x)` is compiled with a static size, it will need\\\\nrecompilation for different sizes:\\\\n\\\\n```{note}\\\\nFor simplicity, this example uses `@torch.compile(dynamic=True)`. Note, that\\\\nthis option is not recommended due to it being error prone.\\\\nFor a recommended way of enabling dynamic shapes, see {ref}`enable-dynamic-behavior`.\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n```{code-cell}\\\\nimport torch\\\\n@torch.compile(dynamic=False)\\\\ndef f(x):\\\\n     return x* x.size()[0]\\\\n\\\\nf(torch.rand(10))\\\\nf(torch.rand(20))\\\\nf(torch.rand(30))\\\\nf(torch.rand(40))\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nIn the produced output, you can see that four graphs were generated.\\\\nSee the corresponding <a href=\\\\\\\"../../_static/img/dynamic_shapes/tlparse1_dynamic_shapes_false.png\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">tlparse output</a>\\\\n\\\\nBy making the size dynamic, the function can handle various sizes without recompilation:\\\\n\\\\n```{code-cell}\\\\nimport torch\\\\n@torch.compile(dynamic=True)\\\\ndef f(x):\\\\n     return x* x.size()[0]\\\\n\\\\nf(torch.rand(10))\\\\nf(torch.rand(20))\\\\nf(torch.rand(30))\\\\nf(torch.rand(40))\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nWith dynamic shapes enabled, only one graph is created. See the\\\\ncorresponding <a href=\\\\\\\"../../_static/img/dynamic_shapes/tlparse2_dynamic_shapes_true.png\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">tlparse output</a>.\\\\n\\\\nWhile compilation time differences\\\\nare minimal for this small example, more complex use cases would show significant\\\\nperformance improvements.\\\\n\\\\n(what_is_a_specialization)=\\\\n## What is a specialization?\\\\n\\\\n**Specialization** refers to optimizing a computational graph for specific input shapes\\\\nby examining shape conditions during control flow. If a branch is taken based on a\\\\nshape condition, the graph is tailored for that condition. If a new input doesn't meet\\\\nthis condition, the system will recompile the graph.\\\\n\\\\nSpecialization allows you to create optimized computational graphs for specific input\\\\nshapes, which can significantly improve execution speed.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n```{code-cell}\\\\nimport torch\\\\n@torch.compile(dynamic=True)\\\\ndef f(x):\\\\n    if x.size()[0] == 10:\\\\n        return x * 10\\\\n\\\\n    if x.size()[0] <= 30:\\\\n        return x*200\\\\n\\\\n    return x*x.size()[0]\\\\n\\\\nf(torch.rand(10))\\\\nf(torch.rand(20))\\\\nf(torch.rand(30))\\\\nf(torch.rand(40))\\\\nf(torch.rand(50))\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nIn the code above, we specialize that the graph requires an input size of 10, in which\\\\ncase it will return `x * 10`. If the input size is less than 30, it will return `x * 200`.\\\\nIn the output, you can see that this creates three graphs.\\\\n\\\\nSee the corresponding <a href=\\\\\\\"../../_static/img/dynamic_shapes/tlparse3_specialization.png\\\\\\\" target=\\\\\\\"_blank\\\\\\\">tlparse output</a>\\\\n\\\\n\\\\nThis is how graphs created for the above function:\\\\n\\\\n```{image} ../../_static/img/dynamic_shapes/dynamic_shapes_example_specialization.png\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n(enable-dynamic-behavior)=\\\\n## Enabling Dynamic Behavior\\\\n\\\\nThere are the following ways to make things dynamic:\\\\n\\\\n* {ref}`automatic_dynamic`\\\\n* {ref}`user_annotations` (preferred)\\\\n* {ref}`torch_compile_dynamic_true` (for testing only)\\\\n* {ref}`dynamic_shapes_advanced_control_options` (for advanced use cases)\\\\n\\\\nRead below about each of this options.\\\\n\\\\n(automatic_dynamic)=\\\\n### Automatic dynamic\\\\n\\\\n**Automatic dynamic** is the default behavior where {func}`torch.compile` performs\\\\nthe initial compilation assuming static shapes are used, while tracking the\\\\ninput sizes from that first compilation. When a recompile is triggered, it\\\\nuses this information to identify which dimensions have changed and marks\\\\nthose as dynamic for the second compilation.\\\\n\\\\n(user_annotations)=\\\\n### User Annotations\\\\n\\\\nSeveral APIs allow users to explicitly mark specific inputs\\\\nby name or code as dynamic. This is useful for avoiding initial compilations that\\\\nwould eventually become dynamic with the previous tools. It is also used to mark\\\\nelements that do not automatically get marked as dynamic, such as neural network\\\\nmodule parameters, and so on. User annotations are the preferred way to enable\\\\ndynamic shapes.\\\\n\\\\n#### `mark_dynamic(tensor, dim, min=min, max=max)`\\\\n\\\\n> ⚠️ **Warning**\\\\n>\\\\n> `torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic()` must not be called inside any function\\\\n> that is being compiled by `torch.compile()` (for example, a model’s\\\\n> `forward()` method or any function it calls).\\\\n>\\\\n> This function is a *tracing-time API*. If it is invoked from within\\\\n> compiled code, Dynamo will raise an error such as:\\\\n>\\\\n> ```\\\\n> AssertionError: Attempt to trace forbidden callable\\\\n> ```\\\\n>\\\\n> **Correct usage** is to call `mark_dynamic` on input tensors *before*\\\\n> invoking `torch.compile`, for example:\\\\n>\\\\n> ```python\\\\n> torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic(x, 0)\\\\n> compiled_model = torch.compile(model)\\\\n> ```\\\\n\\\\n\\\\nThe {func}`torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic` function marks a tensor dimension as dynamic and will fail if it\\\\ngets specialized. It does not work for integers. Use this function only if you know\\\\nall graphs in the frame using this input converge to a single dynamic graph.\\\\nOtherwise, you may encounter a misleading constraint violation error.\\\\nIn such cases, consider using {func}`torch._dynamo.maybe_mark_dynamic`. Currently,\\\\n{func}`torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic`\\\\ndoes not have precedence over `force_parameter_static_shapes = True` or `force_nn_module_property_static_shapes = True`.\\\\n\\\\nIf you know in advance that a particular dimension will be dynamic, you\\\\ncan avoid the initial recompilation by using {func}`torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic(tensor, dim)`.\\\\nAdditionally, if you already know the minimum and maximum possible\\\\nvalues for this dimension, you can specify them with\\\\n{func}`torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic(tensor, dim, min=min, max=max)`.\\\\n\\\\nHere is a quick example:\\\\n\\\\n```{code-cell}\\\\nimport torch\\\\n\\\\n@torch.compile\\\\ndef f(x):\\\\n    return x * x.size()[0]\\\\n\\\\nx = torch.randn(10)\\\\ntorch._dynamo.mark_dynamic(x, 0)\\\\n\\\\n# first invocation we give it is a tensor marked as dynamic\\\\nf(x)\\\\n# rest of these invocations will use dynamically compiled code\\\\nf(torch.randn(20))\\\\nf(torch.randn(30))\\\\nf(torch.randn(40))\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n#### `maybe_mark_dynamic(tensor, dim)`\\\\n\\\\nThe {func}`torch._dynamo.maybe_mark_dynamic` function shares all properties\\\\nwith  {func}`torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic`\\\\nbut does not fail if the size gets specialized. Use it for inputs shared by\\\\nmultiple graphs or if the number of graphs does not converge to one for a specific\\\\nframe. For instance, in the example above, use {func}`torch._dynamo.maybe_mark_dynamic()` because graphs\\\\nwith sizes 0 and 1 will specialize. However, you can use {func}`torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic` to ensure\\\\nyou never specialize.\\\\n\\\\n#### `mark_unbacked(tensor, dim)`\\\\n\\\\nThe {func}`torch._dynamo.decorators.mark_unbacked` function marks a tensor dimension as unbacked. It is unlikely\\\\nto be the tool you need, but it could be useful if the specialization occurs inside\\\\na condition `guard_size_oblivious(x)`, and if using it removes the specialization.\\\\nEnsure it fixes the specialization and does not introduce a data-dependent error\\\\nthat converts to a graph break at or before the specialization location\\\\nyou are trying to  avoid. It might be better to use the next option.\\\\n\\\\n(dynamic_sources_allow_list)=\\\\n#### Dynamic Allow List (`DYNAMIC_SOURCES`)\\\\n\\\\nUse the evnironmental variable `TORCH_COMPILE_DYNAMIC_SOURCES` to pass a configuration\\\\nlist of source names to be marked as dynamic. For example:\\\\n`TORCH_COMPILE_DYNAMIC_SOURCES=L[‘x’],L[‘y’]`\\\\nIt's easiest to find these dynamic source names using the PGO artifact in `tlparse`.\\\\nYou can copy and paste the dynamic source names from the PGO artifact. This method works\\\\nfor integers and tensor sizes and has the highest precedence over all other flags\\\\nthat force static shapes. It will not throw an error if what is marked dynamic\\\\ngets specialized or if the provided input does not exist.\\\\n\\\\nHere is an example:\\\\n\\\\n```{code-cell}\\\\nimport torch\\\\n\\\\n@torch.compile()\\\\ndef f(x):\\\\n     return x * x.size()[0]\\\\n\\\\nwith torch.compiler.config.patch(dynamic_sources=\\\\\\\"L['x']\\\\\\\"):\\\\n    f(torch.rand(10))\\\\nf(torch.rand(20))\\\\nf(torch.rand(30))\\\\nf(torch.rand(40))\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n(torch.compiler.set_stance_eager_then_compile)=\\\\n#### `torch.compiler.set_stance (\\\\\\\"eager_then_compile\\\\\\\")`\\\\n\\\\nAt times, identifying the appropriate inputs to mark as dynamic can\\\\nbe challenging. If you are willing to accept a performance cost for\\\\nthe first batch, another convenient option is to use the\\\\n`eager_then_compile` stances, which automatically determine dynamic\\\\ninputs for you. For more information, see {func}`torch.compiler.set_stance` and [Dynamic Compilation Control with torch.compiler.set_stance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/recipes/torch_compiler_set_stance_tutorial.html).\\\\n\\\\n(torch_compile_dynamic_true)=\\\\n### `torch.compile (dynamic=true)` (Not recommended)\\\\n\\\\nThis setting forces all sizes and integers to be dynamic, increasing the\\\\nchance of encountering dynamic shape bugs. Setting this option is not\\\\nrecommended due to it  being error prone.\\\\nIt would make every input size dynamic which may result it performance\\\\nregressions and ultimately increase compilation time.\\\\n\\\\nPyTorch also provides advanced control options for dynamic shapes, see:\\\\n{ref}`dynamic_shapes_advanced_control_options`.\\\\n\\\\n## Where Do I Go From Here?\\\\n\\\\nIf you encounter a framework code bug or an issue with specialization,\\\\nfile an issue so it can be reviewed and potentially improved. If the issue\\\\nis within your user code, consider whether you are willing to rewrite your\\\\ncode to avoid it. Determine if it affects correctness or if it's a redundant\\\\ncheck. If the issue involves a Triton custom kernel with a `constexpr`\\\\nargument, evaluate whether you can rewrite it to address the problem.\\\\n\\\\n```{toctree}\\\\n:maxdepth: \\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"source_original\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"\\\\n===== docs/source/notes/numerical_accuracy.rst =====\\\\n.. _numerical_accuracy:\\\\n\\\\nNumerical accuracy\\\\n==================\\\\n\\\\nIn modern computers, floating point numbers are represented using IEEE 754 standard.\\\\nFor more details on floating point arithmetic and IEEE 754 standard, please see\\\\n`Floating point arithmetic <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floating-point_arithmetic>`_\\\\nIn particular, note that floating point provides limited accuracy (about 7 decimal digits\\\\nfor single precision floating point numbers, about 16 decimal digits for double precision\\\\nfloating point numbers) and that floating point addition and multiplication are not\\\\nassociative, so the order of the operations affects the results.\\\\nBecause of this, PyTorch is not guaranteed\\\\nto produce bitwise identical results for floating point computations that are\\\\nmathematically identical. Similarly, bitwise identical results are not guaranteed across\\\\nPyTorch releases, individual commits, or different platforms. In particular, CPU and GPU\\\\nresults can be different even for bitwise-identical inputs and even after controlling for\\\\nthe sources of randomness.\\\\n\\\\nBatched computations or slice computations\\\\n------------------------------------------\\\\n\\\\nMany operations in PyTorch support batched computation, where the same operation is performed\\\\nfor the elements of the batches of inputs. An example of this is :meth:`torch.mm` and\\\\n:meth:`torch.bmm`. It is possible to implement batched computation as a loop over batch elements,\\\\nand apply the necessary math operations to the individual batch elements, for efficiency reasons\\\\nwe are not doing that, and typically perform computation for the whole batch. The mathematical\\\\nlibraries that we are calling, and PyTorch internal implementations of operations can produce\\\\nslightly different results in this case, compared to non-batched computations. In particular,\\\\nlet ``A`` and ``B`` be 3D tensors with the dimensions suitable for batched matrix multiplication.\\\\nThen ``(A@B)[0]`` (the first element of the batched result) is not guaranteed to be bitwise\\\\nidentical to ``A[0]@B[0]`` (the matrix product of the first elements of the input batches)\\\\neven though mathematically it's an identical computation.\\\\n\\\\nSimilarly, an operation applied to a tensor slice is not guaranteed to produce results that are\\\\nidentical to the slice of the result of the same operation applied to the full tensor. E.g. let\\\\n``A`` be a 2-dimensional tensor. ``A.sum(-1)[0]`` is not guaranteed to be bitwise equal to\\\\n``A[:,0].sum()``.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\nExtremal values\\\\n---------------\\\\n\\\\nWhen inputs contain large values such that intermediate results may overflow the range of the\\\\nused datatype, the end result may overflow too, even though it is representable in the original\\\\ndatatype. E.g.:\\\\n\\\\n.. code:: python\\\\n\\\\n    import torch\\\\n    a=torch.tensor([1e20, 1e20]) # fp32 type by default\\\\n    a.norm() # produces tensor(inf)\\\\n    a.double().norm() # produces tensor(1.4142e+20, dtype=torch.float64), representable in fp32\\\\n\\\\n.. _Linear Algebra Stability:\\\\n\\\\nLinear algebra (``torch.linalg``)\\\\n---------------------------------\\\\n\\\\nNon-finite values\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nThe external libraries (backends) that ``torch.linalg`` uses provide no guarantees on their behaviour\\\\nwhen the inputs have non-finite values like ``inf`` or ``NaN``. As such, neither does PyTorch.\\\\nThe operations may return a tensor with non-finite values, or raise an exception, or even segfault.\\\\n\\\\nConsider using :func:`torch.isfinite` before calling these functions to detect this situation.\\\\n\\\\nExtremal values in linalg\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nFunctions within ``torch.linalg`` have more `Extremal Values`_ than other PyTorch functions.\\\\n\\\\n:ref:`linalg solvers` and :ref:`linalg inverses` assume that the input matrix ``A`` is invertible. If it is close to\\\\nbeing non-invertible (for example, if it has a very small singular value), then these algorithms may silently return\\\\nincorrect results. These matrices are said to be `ill-conditioned <https://nhigham.com/2020/03/19/what-is-a-condition-number/>`_.\\\\nIf provided with ill-conditioned inputs, the result of these functions they may vary when using the same inputs on different\\\\ndevices or when using different backends via the keyword ``driver``.\\\\n\\\\nSpectral operations like ``svd``, ``eig``, and ``eigh`` may also return incorrect results (and their gradients may be infinite)\\\\nwhen their inputs have singular values that are close to each other. This is because the algorithms used to compute these decompositions\\\\nstruggle to converge for these inputs.\\\\n\\\\nRunning the computation in ``float64`` (as NumPy does by default) often helps, but it does not solve these issues in all cases.\\\\nAnalyzing the spectrum of the inputs via :func:`torch.linalg.svdvals` or their condition number via :func:`torch.linalg.cond`\\\\nmay help to detect these issues.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\nTensorFloat-32(TF32) on Nvidia Ampere (and later) devices\\\\n---------------------------------------------------------\\\\n\\\\nOn Ampere (and later) Nvidia GPUs, PyTorch can use TensorFloat32 (TF32) to speed up mathematically intensive operations, in particular matrix multiplications and convolutions.\\\\nWhen an operation is performed using TF32 tensor cores, only the first 10 bits of the input mantissa are read.\\\\nThis may reduce accuracy and produce surprising results (e.g., multiplying a matrix by the identity matrix may produce results that are different from the input).\\\\nBy default, TF32 tensor cores are disabled for matrix multiplications and enabled for convolutions, although most neural network workloads have the same convergence behavior when using TF32 as they have with fp32.\\\\nWe recommend enabling TF32 tensor cores for matrix multiplications with ``torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = \\\\\\\"tf32\\\\\\\"`` (```torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True`` is going to be deprecated) if your network does not need full float32 precision.\\\\nIf your network needs full float32 precision for both matrix multiplications and convolutions, then TF32 tensor cores can also be disabled for convolutions with ``torch.backends.cudnn.conv.fp32_precision = \\\\\\\"ieee\\\\\\\"`` (``torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False`` is going to be deprecated).\\\\n\\\\nFor more information see :ref:`TensorFloat32<tf32_on_ampere>`.\\\\n\\\\nReduced Precision Reduction for FP16 and BF16 GEMMs\\\\n----------------------------------------------------\\\\nHalf-precision GEMM operations are typically done with intermediate accumulations (reduction) in single-precision for numerical accuracy and improved resilience to overflow. For performance, certain GPU architectures, especially more recent ones, allow a few truncations of the intermediate accumulation results to the reduced precision (e.g., half-precision). This change is often benign from the perspective of model convergence, though it may lead to unexpected results (e.g., ``inf`` values when the final result should be be representable in half-precision).\\\\nIf reduced-precision reductions are problematic, they can be turned off with\\\\n``torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction = False``\\\\n\\\\nA similar flag exists for BF16 GEMM operations and is turned on by default. If BF16\\\\nreduced-precision reductions are problematic, they can be turned off with\\\\n``torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction = False``\\\\n\\\\nFor more information see :ref:`allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction<fp16reducedprecision>` and :ref:`allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction<bf16reducedprecision>`\\\\n\\\\nReduced Precision Reduction for FP16 and BF16 in Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA)\\\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\nA naive SDPA math backend, when using FP16/BF16 inputs, can accumulate significant numerical errors due to the usage of low-precision intermediate buffers. To mitigate this issue, the default behavior now involves upcasting FP16/BF16 inputs to FP32. Computations are performed in FP32/TF32, and the final FP32 results are then downcasted back to FP16/BF16. This will improve numerical accuracy of the final output for the math backend with FP16/BF16 inputs, but increases memory usages and may cause the performance regressions in the math backend as computations shift from FP16/BF16 BMM to FP32/TF32 BMM/Matmul.\\\\n\\\\nFor scenarios where reduced-precision reductions are preferred for speed, they can be enabled with the following setting:\\\\n``torch.backends.cuda.allow_fp16_bf16_reduction_math_sdp(True)``\\\\n\\\\n.. _fp16_on_mi200:\\\\n\\\\nReduced Precision FP16 and BF16 GEMMs and Convolutions on AMD Instinct MI200 devices\\\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\nOn AMD Instinct MI200 GPUs, the FP16 and BF16 V_DOT2 and MFMA matrix instructions flush input and output denormal values to zero. FP32 and FP64 MFMA matrix instructions do not flush input and output denormal values to zero. The affected instructions are only used by rocBLAS (GEMM) and MIOpen (convolution) kernels; all other PyTorch operations will not encounter this behavior. All other supported AMD GPUs will not encounter this behavior.\\\\n\\\\nrocBLAS and MIOpen provide alternate implementations for affected FP16 operations. Alternate implementations for BF16 operations are not provided; BF16 numbers have a larger dynamic range than FP16 numbers and are less likely to encounter denormal values. For the FP16 alternate implementations, FP16 input values are cast to an intermediate BF16 value and then cast back to FP16 output after the accumulate FP32 operations. In this way, the input and output types are unchanged.\\\\n\\\\nWhen training using FP16 precision, some models may fail to converge with FP16 denorms flushed to zero. Denormal values more frequently occur in the backward pass of training during gradient calculation. PyTorch by default will use the rocBLAS and MIOpen alternate implementations during the backward pass. The default behavior can be overridden using environment variables, ROCBLAS_INTERNAL_FP16_ALT_IMPL and MIOPEN_DEBUG_CONVOLUTION_ATTRIB_FP16_ALT_IMPL. The behavior of these environment variables is as follows:\\\\n\\\\n+---------------+-----------+-----------+\\\\n|               | forward   | backward  |\\\\n+===============+===========+===========+\\\\n| Env unset     | original  | alternate |\\\\n+---------------+-----------+-----------+\\\\n| Env set to 1  | alternate | alternate |\\\\n+---------------+-----------+-----------+\\\\n| Env set to 0  | original  | original  |\\\\n+---------------+-----------+-----------+\\\\n\\\\nThe following is the list of operations where rocBLAS may be used:\\\\n\\\\n* torch.addbmm\\\\n* torch.addmm\\\\n* torch.baddbmm\\\\n* torch.bmm\\\\n* torch.mm\\\\n* torch.nn.GRUCell\\\\n* torch.nn.LSTMCell\\\\n* torch.nn.Linear\\\\n* torch.sparse.addmm\\\\n* the following torch._C._ConvBackend implementations:\\\\n\\\\n  * slowNd\\\\n  * slowNd_transposed\\\\n  * slowNd_dilated\\\\n  * slowNd_dilated_transposed\\\\n\\\\nThe following is the list of operations where MIOpen may be used:\\\\n\\\\n* torch.nn.Conv[Transpose]Nd\\\\n* the following torch._C._ConvBackend implementations:\\\\n\\\\n  * ConvBackend::Miopen\\\\n  * ConvBackend::MiopenDepthwise\\\\n  * ConvBackend::MiopenTranspose\\\\n\\\", \\\"excerpt_ranges\\\": [[0, 10998]], \\\"range_unit\\\": \\\"zero-based half-open characters in extracted text\\\", 与状态突变\\\\n\\\\n推理行为不是由一次 eval() 决定的单一状态。模块的 training/eval 行为、自动微分记录、推理区域约束、设备与数值策略、每请求可变状态分别回答不同问题；把“没有梯度”误当成“推理语义正确”，会漏掉随机层、统计量更新、线程上下文和共享状态隔离。\\\\n\\\\n## 问题与状态\\\\n\\\\n把一次前向抽象为 `y_q = f_{θ,T,P}(x_q; R_q)`。`θ` 是模型参数，`x_q` 是请求输入，`P` 是设备、dtype、归约与近似策略，`R_q` 是请求可变状态。这里 `T` 不是根模块的一个布尔值，而是相关模块的模式配置：`T = (t_m)_{m∈M_sens}`，其中 `M_sens` 是 forward 会读取 training 或据其更新 buffer 的模块集合。至少应覆盖 Dropout、BatchNorm 类以及模型自定义的模式分支模块。根模块只是 `M_sens` 的一个元素；根标志正确不能证明某个子模块处于约定模式。\\\\n\\\\n`G` 表示自动微分记录，`I` 表示推理区域深度。`G`/`I` 通常不改变理想实数函数，但决定是否保存反向所需中间量、是否跟踪视图与版本，以及一个张量能否跨区域交给 autograd。若 `T` 中某个相关模块为 train 且含随机算子，该模块还决定随机流，函数输出是一个样本而不是固定值。\\\\n\\\\n| 轴 | 取值或身份 | 主要影响 | 不能由它推断 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| `T` | 相关模块的模式向量，或显式声明的混合模式 | dropout、BatchNorm 统计和模块分支 | 是否记录梯度；根标志是否覆盖所有子模块 |\\\\n| `G` | record / no_grad | 图、保存的中间量、版本/视图簿记 | 模型是否处于 eval |\\\\n| `I` | 推理区域深度 | 关闭部分推理簿记并限制区域张量 | 模型函数自动正确或数值逐位一致 |\\\\n| `P` | device、dtype、归约、近似 | 有限精度、kernel 路径和溢出范围 | 模型语义是否满足任务 |\\\\n| `R_q` | 请求 KV、位置、随机流等 | 单请求状态与并发隔离 | 共享参数是否只读 |\\\\n\\\\n`P` 不是无关紧要的实现细节。TF32 会截短输入尾数并以 FP32 累加；半精度 GEMM 的中间归约可能降精度，SDPA 的不同后端、不同设备归约顺序都可能改变结果；`eval` 只改变模块行为，不保证逐位相同。来源说明明确：种子与确定性配置控制特定路径中的随机性，不保证跨版本、平台和全部算法路径逐位一致。\\\\n\\\\n“状态突变”主要是三类：模块 buffer，例如运行统计；per-request 缓存，例如 KV、位置和随机流计数；共享只读表，例如位置表与常量。模型参数和共享只读表在服务请求中应只读；请求缓存只能由该请求或明确的共享所有者写入。把 KV 或 adapter 状态放进共享模块对象，单请求测试可能通过，并发时会把一个请求的写入泄漏给另一个请求。\\\\n\\\\n状态不变量：\\\\n\\\\n- `T` 在启动时建立并封存。相关模块逐个设置、逐个验证，形成带模块名、类和期望 training 的模式清单；请求入口校验该清单。之后禁止未授权修改；若任务允许混合模式，期望值必须逐模块显式声明。\\\\n- 进入或退出梯度、推理区域只保存并恢复 `G`/`I`，不修改 `T`。恢复失败必须使请求失败，不能把未知上下文带给下一个请求。\\\\n- `I>0` 时创建的张量带有推理区域来源。跨区域交给 autograd 必须经过在推理区域之外建立的合法转换，或有经目标版本核验的显式转换接口；不能只改一个 materialized 布尔值。\\\\n- 请求状态 `R_q` 只有一个写者；其他请求只能读取按契约共享的不可变部分。\\\\n- 异步提交返回不是完成事件；输出、临时区和缓存槽的复用要等待相应 stream/event 与分配器依赖。\\\\n\\\\n空 token、零长度 batch、全 mask 行属于输入边界：选择位置或采样没有定义时，必须返回契约规定的空结果或错误，不能把空张量送进依赖非零 batch 统计的路径。BatchNorm 训练态对零统计量没有合理批统计，应单独处理。\\\\n\\\\n## 合法性与方案选择\\\\n\\\\n模块模式有两种合法配置方式。第一种是统一模式：要求整个相关模块树都取同一 training 值；如果无法枚举会读取 training 的自定义模块，这是更稳妥的契约。第二种是显式混合模式：配置逐项列出每个模式敏感模块的期望值，只有清单声明的模块可以不同。两种方式都不能只检查根模块。\\\\n\\\\n启动时依次执行：解析或声明 `M_sens`；设置每个相关模块的精确模式；如果框架的递归 setter 会覆盖子模块，就先完成统一设置，再逐项恢复显式混合模式；最后快照 `name/class/training` 并封存。服务入口调用清单校验。为了限制运行期修改，模型最好被只读封装或只有启动代码能取得模式 setter；若只能靠检查，至少在每个请求开始和发布结果前比较清单，发现变化就使该请求失败并重新建立模式，不能把已经用未知模式算出的结果当作可服务结果。\\\\n\\\\n- `eval` 与关闭梯度是不同开关。`eval` 让 dropout 等层按评估行为工作，BatchNorm 若配置为使用运行统计则读运行统计；关闭梯度只停止 autograd 记录。服务可以处于 `eval` 且仍记录梯度，也可以处于 `train` 且不记录梯度；后者不是“纯推理”，因为 dropout 和批统计仍可能改变函数或状态。\\\\n- `inference_mode` 不是 `eval` 的替代品。来源说明指出它进一步关闭 view tracking、version counter 等推理簿记，但创建的张量有使用限制；它不会自动把模块切到 eval。\\\\n- 在同一个服务模型实例上按请求切换 training 不是合法隔离方案。该标志是共享对象状态；请求 A 的切换会影响请求 B。应在启动时固定，或为不同行为使用独立实例或独立执行域。\\\\n- 若后处理、adapter 或归因流程需要 autograd，要区分两种范围。仅后处理求导：模型 forward 可以放在推理区域，但必须在所有推理上下文退出后创建普通输出，再在后处理中建立新的记录路径。需要穿过模型求导：必须让模型 forward 处于 record 路径；推理区域已经省略了前向图和保存量，事后 materialize 不能恢复它。\\\\n- 合法转换普通张量的条件是：源张量来自有效推理区域；当前 `I=0`，外层推理上下文也不能仍生效；目标使用新的普通存储，不与源存储别名；复制或转换在非推理区域执行；复制完成事件保护源存储的生命期；异常时释放未发布目标并保留明确的失败状态。若外层 `I>0`，应拒绝或延迟转换；除非目标框架版本有经核验的显式转换接口，不能假定普通复制足够。\\\\n- 数值比较要先固定 `T`、`P`、device、dtype 和输入。`T` 改变时 dropout 或 BatchNorm 可能改变函数，要求 train 与 eval 输出逐位相等不是合法检查；应改为检查各自语义或任务质量。\\\\n- 异步执行下，合法返回只表示工作已入队。若输出缓冲会被复用，必须在消费完成事件之后回收；不同 stream 的读写依赖和 allocator 生命周期需要显式表达。\\\\n\\\\n一个实用的合法性判断是：先问“这个状态改变的是模型函数、autograd 记录、线程上下文，还是请求数据所有权”。改变模型函数的状态不能靠关闭梯度修补；只影响簿记的状态不能拿来证明数值等价；共享对象上的可变状态不能靠调用顺序保证隔离。\\\\n\\\\n## 服务前向的算法与状态变化\\\\n\\\\n下面的状态机把模式变化限制在 worker 的线程上下文中，并把整个相关模块的模式清单当作启动契约而不是每请求开关。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nalgorithm PrepareModelMode(model, mode_spec):\\\\n  # mode_spec: name -> expected training bool，必须精确覆盖 M_sens\\\\n  require mode_spec covers every mode-sensitive module in model\\\\n  for each (name, expected) in mode_spec:\\\\n      m = ResolveModule(model, name)\\\\n      SetTrainingExact(m, expected)\\\\n\\\\n  entries = Snapshot((name, module_class(m), bool(m.training))\\\\n                     for m in ModeSensitiveModules(model))\\\\n  require entries match mode_spec one-to-one\\\\n  return Seal(entries, uniform = false)\\\\n\\\\nalgorithm ValidateFrozenMode(model, sealed_mode):\\\\n  require sealed_mode is sealed\\\\n  live = EnumerateModeSensitive(model)\\\\n  require names(live) = names(sealed_mode.entries)\\\\n  for each (name, expected_class, expected_training) in sealed_mode.entries:\\\\n      m = ResolveModule(model, name)\\\\n      require m exists\\\\n      require module_class(m) = expected_class\\\\n      require bool(m.training) = expected_training\\\\n  return true\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`PrepareModelMode` 中的 `SetTrainingExact` 是目标版本 API 的抽象：如果底层 setter 递归修改子模块，混合模式要在统一设置之后重新应用例外并再次校验。入口不检查“根模块等于一个值”就结束，而是检查完整清单。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nalgorithm PushMode(worker_ctx, kind):\\\\n  saved = (worker_ctx.grad_enabled, worker_ctx.inference_depth)\\\\n\\\\n  if kind = record:\\\\n      if worker_ctx.inference_depth > 0:\\\\n          raise IllegalMode\\\\n      worker_ctx.grad_enabled = true\\\\n  else if kind = no_grad:\\\\n      worker_ctx.grad_enabled = false\\\\n  else if kind = inference:\\\\n      worker_ctx.inference_depth = worker_ctx.inference_depth + 1\\\\n      worker_ctx.grad_enabled = false\\\\n  else:\\\\n      raise InvalidMode\\\\n\\\\n  return saved\\\\n\\\\nalgorithm PopMode(worker_ctx, saved):\\\\n  worker_ctx.grad_enabled = saved.grad_enabled\\\\n  worker_ctx.inference_depth = saved.inference_depth\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`PushMode` 不修改 `T`。`PopMode` 即使前向失败也必须执行，否则 worker 会把一个请求的上下文带给下一个请求。若实现把模式也放进同一个上下文，它必须作为独立所有权处理，不能由梯度相关代码顺带修改。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nalgorithm MaterializeOutsideInference(raw, worker_ctx, stream):\\\\n  require worker_ctx.inference_depth = 0\\\\n  require raw.origin = inference\\\\n\\\\n  out = AllocateOrdinaryStorage(shape=raw.shape,\\\\n                                dtype=raw.dtype,\\\\n                                device=raw.device)\\\\n  require out.storage_id != raw.storage_id\\\\n\\\\n  saved = PushMode(worker_ctx, no_grad)\\\\n  try:\\\\n      CopyData(out, raw)\\\\n      event = RecordCompletion(stream, out)\\\\n  catch error:\\\\n      Release(out)\\\\n      raise error\\\\n  finally:\\\\n      PopMode(worker_ctx, saved)\\\\n\\\\n  out.origin = materialized_after_inference\\\\n  out.model_graph = false\\\\n  out.copy_event = event\\\\n  raw.keep_alive_until = event\\\\n  return out\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n该算法规定：普通存储在推理上下文退出后创建；复制不建立模型前向图；源存储只有在复制完成事件之后才可释放；目标存储不与源别名。若 `worker_ctx.inference_depth > 0`，说明外层推理上下文仍生效，算法拒绝转换。目标框架若另有显式推理张量转换接口，必须按固定版本核对其语义；本章不把“名字叫 materialize”当作自动合法。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nalgorithm ValidateConsumer(t, grad_scope):\\\\n  require t.is_inference = false\\\\n\\\\n  if grad_scope = postprocess_only:\\\\n      require t.origin in {ordinary, materialized_after_inference}\\\\n      require t.copy_event is completed before consumption\\\\n  else if grad_scope = through_model:\\\\n      require t.model_graph = true\\\\n      require t.created_under_record = true\\\\n  else:\\\\n      raise InvalidGradScope\\\\n\\\\n  return true\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`ValidateConsumer` 读取转换产物的实际来源、存储身份、图属性与完成事件，不读取一个自称 materialized 的布尔值。需要穿过模型求导时，`materialized_after_inference` 产物必然缺少模型图，因此被同一 oracle 拒绝。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nalgorithm ServeOne(q, model, cfg, sealed_mode, worker_ctx, stream):\\\\n  require q.owner = q\\\\n  ValidateFrozenMode(model, sealed_mode)\\\\n\\\\n  if q.grad_scope = through_model:\\\\n      require cfg.region_kind = record\\\\n  else if q.grad_scope = postprocess_only:\\\\n      require cfg.region_kind in {inference, no_grad}\\\\n  else:\\\\n      require q.grad_scope = none\\\\n\\\\n  status = Running\\\\n  raw = null\\\\n  z = null\\\\n  error = null\\\\n  saved = PushMode(worker_ctx, cfg.region_kind)\\\\n\\\\n  try:\\\\n      x = NormalizeAndValidate(q.input)\\\\n      y = model.forward(x, q.state)\\\\n      raw = SelectByLogicalPosition(y, q.output_positions)\\\\n      if q.grad_scope = through_model:\\\\n          require raw.model_graph = true\\\\n      status = ForwardDone\\\\n  catch e:\\\\n      status = Failed\\\\n      error = e\\\\n  finally:\\\\n      PopMode(worker_ctx, saved)\\\\n\\\\n  if status = Failed:\\\\n      MarkFailed(q, error)\\\\n      require q.output_not_visible\\\\n      return\\\\n\\\\n  if q.grad_scope = through_model:\\\\n      z = raw\\\\n  else if q.grad_scope = postprocess_only and raw.origin = inference:\\\\n      if worker_ctx.inference_depth > 0:\\\\n          MarkFailed(q, CannotMaterializeUnderOuterInference)\\\\n          return\\\\n      z = MaterializeOutsideInference(raw, worker_ctx, stream)\\\\n  else:\\\\n      z = raw\\\\n\\\\n  if q.downstream_requires_autograd:\\\\n      ValidateConsumer(z, q.grad_scope)\\\\n\\\\n  if not ValidateFrozenMode(model, sealed_mode):\\\\n      MarkFailed(q, ModeMutated)\\\\n      return\\\\n\\\\n  q.pending_output = z\\\\n  PublishAfterCompletion(q, z, stream)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`PopMode` 在 `finally` 中先于后处理和普通存储转换执行；因此转换发生在本次推理区域之外。若仍有外层推理上下文，`MaterializeOutsideInference` 会拒绝，而不是在错误上下文中创建普通张量。发布前再次检查模式清单可以捕获运行期间的意外修改；只能检测检查点的变化，若要求更强保证，应使用只读封装或独立执行域。\\\\n\\\\n请求状态可按下表推进。表描述的是服务契约，不是某个框架内部实现。\\\\n\\\\n| 请求状态 | 允许写入的对象 | 退出条件 | 失败时仍需保护的对象 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| Prepared | 输入缓冲、请求状态分配 | 取得执行槽并固定输入身份 | 尚未提交的输入与已分配槽 |\\\\n| Running | `q.state`、请求本地输出 | 前向提交并且必要时已入队 | 在途 kernel、输入、临时区 |\\\\n| Pending | 输出缓冲、完成事件 | 完成事件到达且输出可读 | 输出所有权与设备消费者 |\\\\n| Committed | 不可再改的请求结果 | 消费者完成或输出被复制 | 仍在读取结果的流或网络层 |\\\\n| Reclaimable | 仅回收记录 | 引用与在途访问都结束 | 延迟完成事件携带的代次 |\\\\n\\\\n失败路径要撤销未提交的状态：不能留下“部分层使用旧权重、部分层使用新状态”的可服务对象。异步返回后立刻释放 `q.state` 也是非法的，除非契约明确保证所有消费者都已结束。\\\\n\\\\n## 成本：计算、访存、通信、准备、同步与驻留\\\\n\\\\n### 逻辑载荷与物理驻留\\\\n\\\\n设某个请求在自动微分路径中保存的中间张量集合为 `S_q`，张量 `a` 的元素数为 `|a|`，每元素 `b_a` 字节，元数据常量 `c_m`。可以定义列举张量的逻辑载荷估算：\\\\n\\\\n`B_logical(q) = Σ_{a∈S_q} |a| · b_a + c_m · |S_q|`。\\\\n\\\\n该式只对 `S_q` 中每个张量的逻辑元素字节求和，可以用于比较同一列举集合的逻辑大小；它不是底层存储驻留、实际设备容量或真实节省的上界。一个小切片可能引用原本很大的底层存储；非连续视图可能跨越比逻辑元素数更大的存储范围；多个保存张量也可能共享同一存储而重复计入上式。\\\\n\\\\n若要计算实际保留容量，应按被引用的底层存储及其同时存活范围计账。设在时刻 `t`，请求 `q` 的保存张量引用的不同存储分配集合为 `A_q(t)`，每个分配 `s` 的驻留计费为 `r_s(t)`，则同时驻留峰值为\\\\n\\\\n`P_peak(q) = max_t Σ_{s∈A_q(t)} r_s(t)`，\\\\n\\\\n其中每个 `s` 只计一次；`r_s` 可以是分配 segment 的字节数，或至少是被引用存储区间的下界。若多个张量共享同一存储，不能按张量个数相加；共享前缀若跨请求共享，还要把物理容量归到唯一所有者并在请求之间避免重复计算。allocator 保留但当前无活跃引用的容量、碎片、元数据和 workspace 另列。\\\\n\\\\n只有在独立紧凑存储假设下，逻辑元素字节才接近物理数据字节：每个 `a` 拥有互不共享的存储，存储恰好容纳 `|a|` 个元素，没有额外 padding 或分配器取整，并且这些存储同时存活。此时\\\\n\\\\n`B_data(q) = Σ_{a∈S_q} |a| · b_a`，\\\\n\\\\n`B_logical` 再加元数据。真实容量仍需把 allocator 容量和碎片另算。\\\\n\\\\n设定一个 FP16 激活为 `8 × 1024 × 4096 × 2 = 67,108,864` 字节，即 64 MiB。若 12 个类似激活各自拥有独立连续存储、同时存活，数据为 `768 MiB`；加每个 16 字节的列举元数据后，`B_logical` 为 `805,306,560` 字节。这里没有计入 allocator 碎片、对齐、workspace、KV 和输出。若 12 个保存量只是同一个 64 MiB 存储上的 12 个单元素切片，逻辑载荷可能只有几百字节，但物理驻留仍可能是 64 MiB；若 12 个保存量都是同一个完整 64 MiB 存储上的视图，逻辑求和可得到 768 MiB，物理驻留却仍是 64 MiB。这个对比说明为什么 `B_logical` 只能作为逻辑列表的估算。\\\\n\\\\n推理区域关闭这一路径的部分保存与版本簿记，但不会删除权重、KV、输出和 kernel workspace；因此不能把上述数值直接当作整段服务的内存节省。实际节省需要比较区域前后仍然存活的底层存储集合，以及 allocator 是否真正回收。\\\\n\\\\n### 计算、同步、准备与驻留\\\\n\\\\ndropout 在训练态生成掩码并执行乘法，设参与元素为 `E_d`；若掩码落内存，还会增加 `E_d · b_mask` 字节。eval 态该层可为恒等，省去随机数、掩码存储和乘法。BatchNorm 若在训练态按 `N × C × H × W` 输入计算批统计，每通道归约 `R = N · H · W` 个元素并更新运行统计；eval 态不再做批归约，只读 `C` 个统计量。额外 `O(E)` 工作不等于额外 `E` 次主存事务，融合、缓存层次和实际布局会改变真实流量。\\\\n\\\\n主机从设备读取一个标量会改变单请求关键路径。设设备工作为 `D`，标量读取发生在 `αD`，主机处理为 `H`，设备到主机的同步延迟为 `L_sync`，末尾主机工作为 `B`。无标量读取时，单请求关键路径可近似为 `D + B`；有读取且没有其他请求填补设备空闲时，近似为\\\\n\\\\n`αD + L_sync + H + (1−α)D + B = D + L_sync + H + B`。\\\\n\\\\n因此在关键路径上增加 `L_sync + H`。取 `D=8 ms`、`H=1 ms`、`L_sync=0.1 ms`，增加约 `1.1 ms`。这是明确设定的解析算例，不是设备实测；吞吐场景中其他请求可能填满空洞，不能用这个单请求数替代吞吐结论。若主机读取发生在设备尚未完成的位置，还会阻止后续提交与设备执行重叠。\\\\n\\\\n编译或图执行若按 `T`、shape、stride、dtype、device、数值策略、状态布局特化成变体，就会产生准备与驻留成本。若冷编译或捕获耗时为 `C_cold`，单次命中节省为 `ΔT`，只按执行时间摊销时门槛为 `N_min > C_cold / ΔT`；加入驻留、缓存失效和首次请求等待后，门槛更高。编译命中率、首次成本和请求分布必须一起记录，不能只统计热路径。\\\\n\\\\n异步执行还有自己的成本：提交、事件记录、跨 stream 等待和分配器的生命周期管理都不直接产生算术，却会改变关键路径。设备调用返回后立即复用输入或输出缓冲，可能让仍在途的 kernel 写坏新请求的数据；这类错误不是“模型数值误差”。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化后的保留、调整与放弃\\\\n\\\\n| 条件变化 | 可以保留 | 应调整或放弃 | 直接检查 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| train 切到 eval，或建立显式混合模式 | 权重、参数布局 | 相关子模块的 training 值；清单和指纹必须重建；输出比较口径要改变 | 根与子模块逐项模式、同一 `T/P` 下的输出 |\\\\n| 后处理需要 autograd | 模型函数与权重 | 若只做后处理，退出推理上下文后建立普通输出；若穿过模型，放弃局部推理区域，改 record | 转换产物的 is_inference、存储身份、完成事件、模型图 |\\\\n| shape/stride/batch 变化 | 数学函数 | 编译桶、guard、图地址和 workspace | 变体 key 与冷/热路径 |\\\\n| dtype、TF32、归约精度变化 | 任务目标 | 数值策略与容差；必要时关闭近似 | 首次分歧、误差尺度、argmax margin |\\\\n| 并发请求增加 | 共享只读参数 | 共享模块上的请求缓存；改为请求本地状态 | 请求交错后的身份与随机流 |\\\\n| 引入新 stream 或异步后处理 | kernel 计算 | 省略的事件依赖与缓冲复用 | event/allocator 生命周期与输出归属 |\\\\n\\\\n如果不打算为 eval 固定模型，就不能声称服务在语义上是纯推理；如果请求缓存无法从共享模块中分离，就应放弃共享可变对象的方案。若 `inference_mode` 的张量限制使后续视图、原地写或 autograd 路径无法合法实现，应改用 no_grad 或普通记录路径，而不是在边界处静默复制一次并假设所有别名和图问题都消失。\\\\n\\\\n数值策略的选择也会反转。若任务只要求任务质量，TF32 或半精度归约可能带来可接受收益；若任务要求接近 FP32 的逐元素精度、极小 logits margin 或可复现实验，近似路径可能必须先被排除。判断依据是参考函数、误差分布和任务质量，而不是 eval 这个名字。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断：竞争解释与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n先固定权重、输入、`P` 和请求状态，再改变一个轴。若 `T` 已经使函数不同，不应要求两种输出逐位相等；若只改变 `G`，确定性算子路径的输出应保持一致，除非代码路径、随机算子或状态突变也变了。\\\\n\\\\n1. **模式树矩阵。** 构造根模块为 eval、某个 Dropout 或 BatchNorm 子模块为 train 的模型。正确的完整清单应在入口拒绝，根模块单点检查会错误通过；后者是必须能触发错误的负对照。再声明一个显式混合模式，让该子模块确实为 train，完整清单应接受。若混合模式被任务允许，不能用“禁止一切混合”代替逐模块验证。\\\\n2. **推理张量转换。** 在同一推理上下文中把 raw 复制成新张量，并标记为 materialized；该产物仍是推理张量，consumer oracle 必须用 is_inference、存储身份和完成事件拒绝它。退出所有推理上下文后创建独立普通存储并复制，postprocess_only 消费者应接受；同一产物送进 through_model 必须因缺少模型图而被拒绝。外层推理深度仍大于零时，转换算法应拒绝或延迟，测试要能区分“外层上下文未退出”和“复制动作失败”。\\\\n3. **保存量口径。** 分别记录列举张量的逻辑元素字节、不同底层存储的容量、allocator reserved 和设备总占用。用一个 64 MiB 存储上的小切片制造“逻辑很小但物理保留很大”，再用多个指向同一存储的完整视图制造“逻辑求和很大但物理只应计一次”。按张量个数累加容量的负对照应重复计算共享存储并被检查器拒绝。\\\\n4. **线程上下文。** 在一个 worker 中嵌套进入 inference 和 no_grad，退出后比较保存的 `G/I`；另一个线程不应继承该上下文。负对照是用全局变量代替线程局部上下文，两个请求交错时会恢复错误状态，且模式可能被意外改写。\\\\n5. **主机同步。** 把设备标量读取改为设备端选择或复制后再在主机处理，保持同一逻辑输出。若设备空洞缩小且延迟下降，支持同步解释；若输出改变，先修复选择语义，不能把结果差异归因给同步。\\\\n6. **请求随机流。** 用 seed、请求身份和逻辑位置生成请求本地序列，比较同一请求单独执行与和其他请求交错执行的结果；请求本地序列应相同，全局随机流会随调度改变。这个反例能区分“采样算法错”和“随机流共享错”。\\\\n7. **数值与结构错误。** 切换 TF32、半精度归约或归约顺序，比较最大误差、分位数、首次分歧层和 argmax margin。小误差在 margin 很小时换 token 是数值解释；轴、mask 或权重布局错误通常产生更大的结构分歧，不能靠放宽容差修复。负对照是故意转置一个权重布局，检查器应把它拒绝，而不是把它当作普通舍入误差。\\\\n8. **编译与图路径。** 比较冷启动、热命中、shape 变化和模式变化后的变体数量；若每次请求切换模式都产生新变体，说明变体 key 或使用方式有问题。再与同 `T/P` 的 eager 路径比较，区分编译收益和状态错误。\\\\n\\\\n竞争解释需要不同预测。例如“eval 后仍随机”可能来自某个子模块仍是 train、请求级随机流未绑定、主机前处理有随机性或设备算法不确定；完整模式清单只固定相关模块，固定后仍变化才支持更底层的非确定性解释。“推理模式内存下降”也可能只是活跃张量下降而 allocator 尚未归还；需要把逻辑载荷、底层存储引用和物理容量分开记录。\\\\n\\\\n## 接入与验证边界\\\\n\\\\n模型接入时应把 `T`、`P`、device、dtype 和请求状态布局作为显式配置，而不是依赖初始化线程的临时状态。模式清单必须覆盖所有会读取 training 的层；对无法枚举的自定义模块，采用统一模式并对完整模块树建立指纹。预热要覆盖计划服务的同一模式、同一数值策略和代表性 shape；第一次真实输入可能创建位置表、选择算法或扩容共享 buffer。共享 buffer 扩容时，其他线程不应读取尚未发布完整的新对象；不可变版本替换或明确同步比依赖调用顺序更容易验证。\\\\n\\\\n权重加载、模块模式和数值策略是不同契约。shape 相同不能证明语义相同；转置权重、不同 epsilon、不同激活近似或不同 dtype 都可能改变函数。原生扩展还需要约定 shape、stride、dtype、device、当前 stream、输出别名和 workspace 生命周期；扩展没有显式建立依赖时，eager 单线程成功不能证明并发安全。\\\\n\\\\n本章的公式、模式状态机、存储账和算例是机制推导与设定模型，不是目标 GPU 上的时间、内存或质量实测。CPU 上的小模型检查可以验证模式清单、推理张量转换的抽象状态、逻辑/物理存储口径和请求随机流，但不能替代目标设备的 kernel、stream、allocator 和服务尾延迟验证；通过检查也不能据此声称 Agent 的构建能力或模型质量已经改善。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- \\\"candidate.json\\\": {\\\"chapter\\\": \\\"# K-FW-001：PyTorch 推理：模块模式、Autograd 与状态突变\\\\n\\\\n推理行为不是由一次 `eval()` 决定的单一状态。模块的 training/eval 行为、自动微分记录、推理区域约束、设备与数值策略、每请求可变状态分别回答不同问题；把“没有梯度”误当成“推理语义正确”，会漏掉随机层、统计量更新、线程上下文和共享状态隔离。\\\\n\\\\n## 问题与状态\\\\n\\\\n把一次前向抽象为 `y_q = f_{θ,T,P}(x_q; R_q)`。`θ` 是模型参数，`x_q` 是请求输入，`T` 是模块的 training/eval 行为状态，`P` 是设备、dtype、归约与近似策略，`R_q` 是请求可变状态。`G` 表示自动微分记录，`I` 表示推理区域深度。`G`/`I` 通常不改变理想实数函数，但决定是否保存反向所需中间量、是否跟踪视图与版本，以及一个张量能否跨区域交给 autograd。若 `T=train` 且层含随机算子，`T` 还决定随机流，函数输出是一个样本而不是固定值。\\\\n\\\\n| 轴 | 取值或身份 | 主要影响 | 不能由它推断 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| `T` | train / eval | dropout、BatchNorm 统计和模块分支 | 是否记录梯度 |\\\\n| `G` | record / no_grad | 图、保存的中间量、版本/视图簿记 | 模型是否处于 eval |\\\\n| `I` | 推理区域深度 | 关闭部分推理簿记并限制区域张量 | 模型函数自动正确或数值逐位一致 |\\\\n| `P` | device、dtype、归约、近似 | 有限精度、kernel 路径和溢出范围 | 模型语义是否满足任务 |\\\\n| `R_q` | 请求 KV、位置、随机流等 | 单请求状态与并发隔离 | 共享参数是否只读 |\\\\n\\\\n`P` 不是无关紧要的实现细节。TF32 会截短输入尾数并以 FP32 累加，半精度 GEMM 的中间归约降精度、SDPA 的不同后端、不同设备归约顺序都可能改变结果；`eval` 只改变模块行为，不保证逐位相同。来源说明明确：种子与确定性配置控制特定路径中的随机性，不保证跨版本、平台和全部算法路径逐位一致。\\\\n\\\\n“状态突变”主要是三类：模块 buffer，例如运行统计；per-request 缓存，例如 KV、位置和随机流计数；共享只读表，例如位置表与常量。模型参数和共享只读表在服务请求中应只读；请求缓存只能由该请求或明确的共享所有者写入。把 KV 或 adapter 状态放进共享模块对象，单请求测试可能通过，并发时会把一个请求的写入泄漏给另一个请求。\\\\n\\\\n状态不变量：\\\\n\\\\n- 进入或退出梯度、推理区域只保存并恢复 `G`/`I`，不修改 `T`。\\\\n- `I>0` 时若不要求 autograd，也不能把区域创建的张量当作普通长期对象；跨区域消费必须经过明确的 materialize 或所有权转移。\\\\n- 请求状态 `R_q` 只有一个写者；其他请求只能读取按契约共享的不可变部分。\\\\n- 异步提交返回不是完成事件；输出、临时区和缓存槽的复用要等待相应 stream/event 与分配器依赖。\\\\n\\\\n空 token、零长度 batch、全 mask 行属于输入边界：选择位置或采样没有定义时，必须返回契约规定的空结果或错误，不能把空张量送进依赖非零 batch 统计的路径。BatchNorm 训练态对零统计量没有合理批统计，应单独处理。\\\\n\\\\n## 合法性与方案选择\\\\n\\\\n- `eval` 与关闭梯度是不同开关。`eval` 让 dropout 等层按评估行为工作，BatchNorm 若配置为使用运行统计则读运行统计；关闭梯度只停止 autograd 记录。服务可以处于 `eval` 且仍记录梯度，也可以处于 `train` 且不记录梯度；后者不是“纯推理”，因为 dropout 和批统计仍可能改变函数或状态。\\\\n- `inference_mode` 不是 `eval` 的替代品。来源说明指出它进一步关闭 view tracking、version counter 等推理簿记，但创建的张量有使用限制；它不会自动把模块切到 eval。\\\\n- 在同一个服务模型实例上按请求切换 `training` 不是合法隔离方案。该标志是共享对象状态；请求 A 的切换会影响请求 B。应在启动时固定，或为不同行为使用独立实例或独立执行域。\\\\n- 若后处理、adapter 或归因流程需要 autograd，推理区域只能覆盖不需要记录的那一段。跨边界应显式 materialize 成普通输出，或在区域外重新进入记录路径；不能忽略框架对区域张量的限制。\\\\n- 数值比较要先固定 `T`、`P`、device、dtype 和输入。`T` 改变时 dropout 或 BatchNorm 可能改变函数，要求 train 与 eval 输出逐位相等不是合法检查；应改为检查各自语义或任务质量。\\\\n- 异步执行下，合法返回只表示工作已入队。若输出缓冲会被复用，必须在消费完成事件之后回收；不同 stream 的读写依赖和 allocator 生命周期需要显式表达。\\\\n\\\\n一个实用的合法性判断是：先问“这个状态改变的是模型函数、autograd 记录、线程上下文，还是请求数据所有权”。改变模型函数的状态不能靠关闭梯度修补；只影响簿记的状态不能拿来证明数值等价；共享对象上的可变状态不能靠调用顺序保证隔离。\\\\n\\\\n## 服务前向的算法与状态变化\\\\n\\\\n下面的状态机把模式变化限制在 worker 的线程上下文中，并把模型 training 状态当作启动契约而不是每请求开关。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nalgorithm PushMode(worker_ctx, kind):\\\\n  saved = (worker_ctx.grad_enabled,\\\\n           worker_ctx.inference_depth,\\\\n           worker_ctx.module_training)\\\\n\\\\n  if kind = record:\\\\n      if worker_ctx.inference_depth > 0:\\\\n          raise IllegalMode\\\\n      worker_ctx.grad_enabled = true\\\\n  else if kind = no_grad:\\\\n      worker_ctx.grad_enabled = false\\\\n  else if kind = inference:\\\\n      worker_ctx.inference_depth = worker_ctx.inference_depth + 1\\\\n      worker_ctx.grad_enabled = false\\\\n  else:\\\\n      raise InvalidMode\\\\n\\\\n  return saved\\\\n\\\\nalgorithm PopMode(worker_ctx, saved):\\\\n  require worker_ctx.module_training = saved.module_training\\\\n  worker_ctx.grad_enabled = saved.grad_enabled\\\\n  worker_ctx.inference_depth = saved.inference_depth\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`PushMode` 不修改 `module_training`。`PopMode` 即使前向失败也必须执行，否则 worker 会把一个请求的上下文带给下一个请求。若实现把训练标志也放进同一个上下文，它必须作为独立所有权处理，不能由梯度相关代码顺带修改。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\nalgorithm ServeOne(q, model, cfg):\\\\n  require q.owner = q\\\\n  require model.training = cfg.module_training\\\\n  saved = PushMode(worker_ctx, cfg.region_kind)\\\\n\\\\n  try:\\\\n      x = NormalizeAndValidate(q.input)\\\\n      y = model.forward(x, q.state)\\\\n      z = SelectByLogicalPosition(y, q.output_positions)\\\\n\\\\n      if q.downstream_requires_autograd:\\\\n          z = MaterializeForAutograd(z, q)\\\\n\\\\n      q.pending_output = z\\\\n      PublishAfterCompletion(q, z)\\\\n  catch error:\\\\n      MarkFailed(q, error)\\\\n      require q.output_not_visible\\\\n  finally:\\\\n      PopMode(worker_ctx, saved)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n`MaterializeForAutograd` 表示把区域结果复制或转换成普通输出，并建立新的所有权；具体接口和允许的转换方式必须按实际框架版本核对，不能把“名字叫 materialize”当作自动合法。若区域张量本身已受限制，继续把它当作 autograd 输入会在边界之后才暴露错误。\\\\n\\\\n请求状态可按下表推进。表描述的是服务契约，不是某个框架内部实现。\\\\n\\\\n| 请求状态 | 允许写入的对象 | 退出条件 | 失败时仍需保护的对象 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| Prepared | 输入缓冲、请求状态分配 | 取得执行槽并固定输入身份 | 尚未提交的输入与已分配槽 |\\\\n| Running | `q.state`、请求本地输出 | 前向提交并且必要时已入队 | 在途 kernel、输入、临时区 |\\\\n| Pending | 输出缓冲、完成事件 | 完成事件到达且输出可读 | 输出所有权与设备消费者 |\\\\n| Committed | 不可再改的请求结果 | 消费者完成或输出被复制 | 仍在读取结果的流或网络层 |\\\\n| Reclaimable | 仅回收记录 | 引用与在途访问都结束 | 延迟完成事件携带的代次 |\\\\n\\\\n失败路径要撤销未提交的状态：不能留下“部分层使用旧权重、部分层使用新状态”的可服务对象。异步返回后立刻释放 `q.state` 也是非法的，除非契约明确保证所有消费者都已结束。\\\\n\\\\n## 成本：计算、访存、准备、同步与驻留\\\\n\\\\n设某个请求在自动微分路径中保存的中间张量集合为 `S_q`，张量 `a` 的元素数为 `|a|`，每元素 `b_a` 字节，元数据常量 `c_m`。一个可检查的上界是\\\\n\\\\n`B_saved(q) = Σ_{a∈S_q} |a| · b_a + c_m · |S_q|`。\\\\n\\\\n设定一个 FP16 激活为 `8 × 1024 × 4096 × 2 = 64 MiB`。若 12 个类似激活同时存活，仅这些张量为 `768 MiB`；这还不含 allocator 碎片、workspace 和未被列出的临时量。推理区域关闭这一路径的部分保存与版本簿记，但不会删除权重、KV、输出和 kernel workspace；因此不能把上述数值直接当作整段服务的内存节省。\\\\n\\\\ndropout 在训练态生成掩码并执行乘法，设参与元素为 `E_d`；若掩码落内存，还会增加 `E_d · b_mask` 字节。eval 态该层可为恒等，省去随机数、掩码存储和乘法。BatchNorm 若在训练态按 `N × C × H × W` 输入计算批统计，每通道归约 `R = N · H · W` 个元素并更新运行统计；eval 态不再做批归约，只读 `C` 个统计量。额外 `O(E)` 工作不等于额外 `E` 次主存事务，融合、缓存层次和实际布局会改变真实流量。\\\\n\\\\n主机从设备读取一个标量会改变单请求关键路径。设设备工作为 `D`，标量读取发生在 `αD`，主机处理为 `H`，设备到主机的同步延迟为 `L_sync`，末尾主机工作为 `B`。无标量读取时，单请求关键路径可近似为 `D + B`；有读取且没有其他请求填补设备空闲时，近似为\\\\n\\\\n`αD + L_sync + H + (1−α)D + B = D + L_sync + H + B`。\\\\n\\\\n因此在关键路径上增加 `L_sync + H`。取 `D=8 ms`、`H=1 ms`、`L_sync=0.1 ms`，增加约 `1.1 ms`。这是明确设定的解析算例，不是设备实测；吞吐场景中其他请求可能填满空洞，不能用这个单请求数替代吞吐结论。若主机读取发生在设备尚未完成的位置，还会阻止后续提交与设备执行重叠。\\\\n\\\\n编译或图执行若按 `T`、shape、stride、dtype、device、数值策略、状态布局特化成变体，就会产生准备与驻留成本。若冷编译或捕获耗时为 `C_cold`，单次命中节省为 `ΔT`，只按执行时间摊销时门槛为 `N_min > C_cold / ΔT`；加入驻留、缓存失效和首次请求等待后，门槛更高。编译命中率、首次成本和请求分布必须一起记录，不能只统计热路径。\\\\n\\\\n异步执行还有自己的成本：提交、事件记录、跨 stream 等待和分配器的生命周期管理都不直接产生算术，却会改变关键路径。设备调用返回后立即复用输入或输出缓冲，可能让仍在途的 kernel 写坏新请求的数据；这类错误不是“模型数值误差”。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化后的保留、调整与放弃\\\\n\\\\n| 条件变化 | 可以保留 | 应调整或放弃 | 直接检查 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| train 切到 eval | 权重、参数布局 | dropout 随机路径、批统计更新；输出比较口径要改变 | worker 起始状态、同一 `T/P` 下的输出 |\\\\n| 后处理需要 autograd | 模型函数与权重 | 受影响边界的推理区域；改为区域外记录或显式 materialize | 区域张量是否被错误送进 autograd |\\\\n| shape/stride/batch 变化 | 数学函数 | 编译桶、guard、图地址和 workspace | 变体 key 与冷/热路径 |\\\\n| dtype、TF32、归约精度变化 | 任务目标 | 数值策略与容差；必要时关闭近似 | 首次分歧、误差尺度、argmax margin |\\\\n| 并发请求增加 | 共享只读参数 | 共享模块上的请求缓存；改为请求本地状态 | 请求交错后的身份与随机流 |\\\\n| 引入新 stream 或异步后处理 | kernel 计算 | 省略的事件依赖与缓冲复用 | event/allocator 生命周期与输出归属 |\\\\n\\\\n如果不打算为 eval 固定模型，就不能声称服务在语义上是纯推理；如果请求缓存无法从共享模块中分离，就应放弃共享可变对象的方案。若 `inference_mode` 的张量限制使后续视图、原地写或 autograd 路径无法合法实现，应改用 `no_grad` 或普通区域，而不是在边界处静默复制一次并假设所有别名问题都消失。\\\\n\\\\n数值策略的选择也会反转。若任务只要求任务质量，TF32 或半精度归约可能带来可接受收益；若任务要求接近 FP32 的逐元素精度、极小 logits margin 或可复现实验，近似路径可能必须先被排除。判断依据是参考函数、误差分布和任务质量，而不是 `eval` 这个名字。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断：竞争解释与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n先固定权重、输入、`P` 和请求状态，再改变一个轴。若 `T` 已经使函数不同，不应要求两种输出逐位相等；若只改变 `G`，确定性算子路径的输出应保持一致，除非代码路径、随机算子或状态突变也变了。\\\\n\\\\n1. **模式矩阵。** 用固定线性模块和输入比较 `(T,G)` 的四种组合；纯线性算子不应因 `G` 改变而改变数值。再加入 dropout 或 BatchNorm，trian/eval 的差异才应出现。负对照是故意让模型保持 train 但声称处于 eval：worker 起始检查必须拒绝；若检查只验证“梯度已关闭”，它会错误通过。\\\\n2. **线程上下文。** 在一个 worker 中嵌套进入 inference 和 no_grad，退出后比较保存的 `G/I`；另一个线程不应继承该上下文。负对照是用全局变量代替线程局部上下文，两个请求交错时会恢复错误状态，且 `training` 可能被意外改写。\\\\n3. **主机同步。** 把设备标量读取改为设备端选择或复制后再在主机处理，保持同一逻辑输出。若设备空洞缩小且延迟下降，支持同步解释；若输出改变，先修复选择语义，不能把结果差异归因给同步。\\\\n4. **内存口径。** 分别记录活跃 tensor 字节、allocator 保留量和设备总占用。推理路径可能显著降低第一项，却不立即降低第二项；只观察 reserved 或 RSS 不能区分图内存、缓存保留和碎片。负对照是把 reserved 当作活跃对象并宣称“推理模式没有省内存”。\\\\n5. **请求随机流。** 用 `seed`、请求身份和逻辑位置生成请求本地序列，比较同一请求单独执行与和其他请求交错执行的结果；请求本地序列应相同，全局随机流会随调度改变。这个反例能区分“采样算法错”和“随机流共享错”。\\\\n6. **数值与结构错误。** 切换 TF32、半精度归约或归约顺序，比较最大误差、分位数、首次分歧层和 argmax margin。小误差在 margin 很小时换 token 是数值解释；轴、mask 或权重布局错误通常产生更大的结构分歧，不能靠放宽容差修复。负对照是故意转置一个权重布局，检查器应把它拒绝，而不是把它当作普通舍入误差。\\\\n7. **编译与图路径。** 比较冷启动、热命中、shape 变化和 mode 变化后的变体数量；若每次请求切换模式都产生新变体，说明变体 key 或使用方式有问题。再与同 `T/P` 的 eager 路径比较，区分编译收益和状态错误。\\\\n\\\\n竞争解释需要不同预测。例如“eval 后仍随机”可能来自模型仍有训练层、请求级随机流未绑定、主机前处理有随机性或设备算法不确定；固定 `T` 并关闭随机算子后仍变化，才支持更底层的非确定性解释。“推理模式内存下降”也可能只是活跃张量下降而 allocator 尚未归还；需要把对象生命周期和物理容量分开记录。\\\\n\\\\n## 接入与验证边界\\\\n\\\\n模型接入时应把 `T`、`P`、device、dtype 和请求状态布局作为显式配置，而不是依赖初始化线程的临时状态。预热要覆盖计划服务的同一模式、同一数值策略和代表性 shape；第一次真实输入可能创建位置表、选择算法或扩容共享 buffer。共享 buffer 扩容时，其他线程不应读取尚未发布完整的新对象；不可变版本替换或明确同步比依赖调用顺序更容易验证。\\\\n\\\\n权重加载、模块模式和数值策略是不同契约。shape 相同不能证明语义相同；转置权重、不同 epsilon、不同激活近似或不同 dtype 都可能改变函数。原生扩展还需要约定 shape、stride、dtype、device、当前 stream、输出别名和 workspace 生命周期；扩展没有显式建立依赖时，eager 单线程成功不能证明并发安全。\\\\n\\\\n本章的公式、模式状态机和算例是机制推导与设定模型，不是目标 GPU 上的时间、内存或质量实测。CPU 上的小模型检查可以验证模式恢复、请求随机流和成本恒等式，但不能替代目标设备的 kernel、stream、allocator 和服务尾延迟验证；通过检查也不能据此声称 Agent 的构建能力或模型质量已经改善。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-TORCH-INFERENCE：PyTorch — inference_mode](../sources/S-TORCH-INFERENCE.md)：inference_mode 关闭推理不需要的 autograd 的内容应是经过核对的算法伪代码、数据流、状态关系与条件化事实，不能把整个实现文件称作知识原文。文档/源码混合资料按实际内容选择可读文档；文件扩展名、压缩包形式和仓库名称本身不决定知识价值。已有源码归档可以保留供溯源审计，其字节和哈希不因来源说明修订而改变。\\\\n\\\\n正文引用需要带实质内容，再指向来源说明；来源说明指向可读论文或文档。必要内容离线可读，不依赖 Agent 联网补全。准确版本留作证据身份；只有影响本题合法性或成本的版本事实进入论证，不搬运与本题无关的参数和分支。\\\\n\\\\n## 逐层阅读\\\\n\\\\n阅读入口按主题地图、章节摘要与问题/前提、二级节结构、完整论证、来源原文展开。Agent 自主选择阅读深度；索引与检索结果提供相邻机制，不产生必读清单。读取按实际字符范围与冻结修订记录；读过摘要不等于读过整章。\\\\n\\\\n## Base、观测和 workflow\\\\n\\\\nBase 的来源事实受发布版本的时间上限约束；编辑日期不改变事实日期。新的整理和独立推导保留真实日期与依据，后续实验不能伪装成历史 seed。\\\\n\\\\n运行观测保存环境、workload、测量方法、数值/单位/不确定性、实验证据与真实日期。机制知识解释因果、条件、预测和反例。Workflow 保存一类局部设计、诊断或验证问题的触发条件、前提、步骤、检查与退出/调整条件、成本和复用边界。三者相互引用，不能用一次成功代替机制解释或跨条件验证。\\\\n\\\\nEvolution 提炼、Diagnostician 独立复核，沿已有发布和证据机制进入后续冻结、检索与读取。Workflow 为可选方法，不自动成为 Controller 的全局顺序。跨任务资格使用现有权威晋升机制，负面与不确定结果保留，不建立平行资格体系。\\\\n\\\\n## 修订、覆盖和验证\\\\n\\\\n已有技术对象优先深化原章；独立对象才新增章节。修订保存登记前正文与元数据的准确字节，更新 catalog、来源说明哈希、导航、时间审计、VERSION 与变更清单。已存在的来源归档保持原身份。\\\\n\\\\n覆盖审计同时检查能力域、具体算法与跨机制组合，区分完整解释、仅提及、缺少推导、缺少证据和缺失；篇数和术语命中不是覆盖证明。结构/身份检查、独立算法算例、运行时读取/发布测试与真实构建效果分别报告。通过前几项不能声称已证明知识改善了 Agent 的系统设计或性能。\\\\n\\\\n六项标准的具体追问、组合案例、来源核对和使用效果边界见[知识内容审查](knowledge-review.md)。[Attention 模块](attention-module.md)是内容深度的已完成样例；其算法、硬件映射与组合状态按主题选择展开，不规定所有专题复制同样的结构。逐篇扩展状态见[扩展状态](expansion-status.json)，导航登记不代表深度验收完成。\\\\n\\\\n连续构建按[知识库构建 workflow](knowledge-build-workflow.md)执行：保存当前基线、分配专题、独立审查、真实检查、修订和统一登记；全库队列保留未完成项。固定的是输入、交付物与证据边界，内容是否充分仍需针对当前论证判断。\\\\n\\\", \\\"excerpt_ranges\\\": [[0, 2251]], \\\"range_unit\\\": \\\"zero-based \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"required\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# 知识内容审查：从 Attention 样例推广\\\\n\\\\n本页把 Attention 多轮审查发现的问题整理为内容作者与审阅者可复用的问题。依据是[知识库构建方法](knowledge-method.md)中的六项标准，深度样例是[当前 Attention 模块](attention-module.md)。它不增加 Agent 的角色义务，也不要求每章采用同一结构、同样多的算例或统一的工程路线。\\\\n\\\\n## 知识库承担什么任务\\\\n\\\\n本库支持 InfraAgents 根据模型、workload、硬件和服务目标，从空工程构建、检验与持续优化完整推理系统。知识应提供五种帮助：还原问题的理论基础；区分合法条件与可探索的设计空间；给出足以独立实现的算法与状态关系；支持成本预测、实验和诊断；保存能够被反驳、修正和迁移的经验。\\\\n\\\\n一条有用的阅读链应支持读者形成这样的推理：任务与输入条件 → 正确性要求 → 候选算法与数据流 → 成本预测 → 区分实验 → 实现结果 → 修正后的结论。某一章可以承担其中一部分，但承担核心算法的地方不能只列注意事项或把关键步骤交给源码。\\\\n\\\\n## 六项标准怎样落实到实际问题\\\\n\\\\n| 内容标准 | 审阅时实际追问 | 过去发现的问题及其含义 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 原因、数学定义、输入输出和状态 | 为什么需要这个机制？每个量的轴、单位、范围和身份是什么？状态代表已知、已算、已确认还是已分配？ | FP8 只写“使用块尺度”不足以恢复分数和 PV 的共同单位；调度中的 token 已生成不等于其 KV 已计算 |\\\\n| 合法性与方案选择 | 哪条性质来自函数、数值契约或设备语义，哪条来自某个方案？等价性在实数、浮点还是特定误差范围内成立？ | 精确算术的归约结合性不能直接变成浮点逐位相同；图地址稳定不证明数据身份仍正确；内部 fragment 未公开就不能猜 lane 映射 |\\\\n| 算法、数据流和状态变化 | 能否写出初始化、推进、提交和结束？第一块、最后一块、空输入和失败分支怎样处理？每个被消费的量从哪里产生？ | 量化流程需要量化与恢复尺度；缓冲需要生产者、所有消费者及代次；硬件专题需要一条从逻辑 tile 到地址、线程、片上布局、指令输入和写回的完整路径 |\\\\n| 六类成本 | 是否在同一候选、相同输入和相同时间范围中列账？哪些量可以相加，哪些受关键路径和共享资源限制？ | 唯一 KV、各 head 请求流量和 DRAM 事务不能混算；共享容量只计一次；预留池与其中存活对象不能重复相加；深流水的驻留和 spill 会改变本来用于估时的吞吐 |\\\\n| 条件变化后的选择 | 改变 shape、状态组织、精度、到达轨迹或设备能力，哪条依赖保留，哪项成本改变？何种结果足以推翻原选择？ | 更多分区在并行度不足时有利，在已经饱和时可能只增加合并；更多缓冲不保证更快；缓存命中不保证新请求可立即执行 |\\\\n| 区分竞争解释 | 观察支持哪些解释？它们对某个可控改变给出什么不同预测？实验结果不符后怎样修改判断？ | “三级比两级慢”同时允许首尾、spill、驻留和未重叠解释；一次时间测量不能决定原因；软件事件模型不能证明 GPU 的内存可见性 |\\\\n\\\\n这些问题由主题决定使用范围。调度章节需要把就绪性、预算和输出归属连起来；缓存章节需要贯通身份、复制、发布和回收；硬件章节需要贯通布局、执行契约和资源。协议、统计或模型语义章节不必凭空增加矩阵指令实例。\\\\n\\\\n## 从单个机制走到组合案例\\\\n\\\\n分开解释各个机制之后，选择会改变合法性或成本的真实交界，追踪一次完整变化。例如共享前缀和私有尾块在追加、封存、发布、消费与回收期间，内容、scale、页表和读者必须属于一致的状态；调度器选中的工作必须已有上游输入和容量，而执行视图的压紧不能改变请求归属。\\\\n\\\\n审阅者沿一次轨迹检查：发生了什么输入事件；哪些对象仍存活；谁能写；谁已经取得读取权；何时对消费者可见；失败后哪些旧状态仍有效；取消后哪些工作仍在途；何时能把同一物理资源交给下一使用者。对象需要身份或代次时，解释防止的具体错误。只有单次同步执行的算法不必引入多代次协议。\\\\n\\\\n交界还包括“看似已经完成，下一步却没有输入”的状态。本轮调度审阅发现：完整命中 KV 而没有末行 logits 时，只按已知长度减 KV 长度选择工作会得到零，无法生成第一个新 token。修订明确了安全重算最后一个已知 token 的路径及共享写区隔离。沿状态图检查是否存在有合法请求却无后继事件的停滞，比只检查各状态的字段范围更有用。\\\\n\\\\n组合案例应使读者能计算至少一项会影响决定的代价，并解释另一种选择何时反转。重点是让独立机制能够正确拼接，不是枚举所有组合。示例的页长、tile、队列策略和版本字段均为可替换选择。\\\\n\\\\n## 阅读链与事实核对\\\\n\\\\n先检查正文承担的核心知识，再检查直接来源说明与足以支持关键事实的固定论文或文档。保留原始资料的错误、版本身份和字节，在解释中纠正公式或限定结论；自己的推导不能归为论文实测。源码可以用于作者核对，但读者独立实现所需的事实应进入允许读取的算法说明。\\\\n\\\\n审查记录写明读过哪些正文、哪些来源及其范围、发现的具体问题、实际修改与检查。只有读取摘要、术语检索或运行链接检查的专题，继续保留深度复核待完成状态。没有必要为了一个确定问题递归阅读所有引用。\\\\n\\\\n## 内容与使用效果分别验收\\\\n\\\\n内容审查判断六项标准在声明范围内是否有充分解释。作者侧算例验证代数、布局、边界、协议或成本模型；它需要独立参考、不变量或能触发错误的负对照，不能只让测试复述实现。读取测试检查冻结内容能否被取回及身份是否匹配。这三类证据各自有效，不能互相代替。\\\\n\\\\n直接使用检验让 Agent 在没有现成实现的情况下处理正文未直接演示的问题：重新推导合法算法，改变输入或硬件条件后重算，面对错误提出竞争解释，收到反证后修改方案。保存允许资料、任务、模型/上下文、预算、答卷或实现、执行结果及失败归因。交叉审阅兼做推导练习可以发现内容缺口，但有共同上下文、作者经验或未隔离的环境时，只能声称完成这次练习。\\\\n\\\\n如果要声称“知识改善了 Agent 的构建能力”，还需可比的知识版本或对照条件、多个代表任务以及预先说明的判断方法。目标 GPU 的数值、同步、重叠和性能仍需设备结果。没有最佳 tile 或流水级数不构成知识缺陷；没有解释如何推导候选、识别限制、测量与修正，才是内容缺口。\\\\n\\\\n## 怎样给出审查结论\\\\n\\\\n对每个问题给出正文位置、明确结论与证据边界，区分“已完整解释”“仅提及”“缺推导”“缺证据”“缺失”。这些描述可按实际内容组合使用，不转成总分或用测试数量抵消关键算法缺口。\\\\n\\\\n已经修复的问题在新修订中复核后关闭，不沿用旧审查中“仍缺 FP8/硬件映射/组合案例”的判断。新的缺口必须来自当前字节。Attention 当前的两个具体案例已补足内容展开，实际 Agent 独立构建与目标 GPU 效果仍有各自的验证边界。以当前内容和当前证据决定结论，不为了持续审查而不断增加验收条件。\\\\n\\\\n扩展工作优先完成相关专题的一条知识链，再复核跨专题衔接。当前批次与逐篇状态见[扩展状态](expansion-status.json)；历史审查保留当时结论，不覆盖成当前状态。\\\\n\\\",
